new.title: Alignment-driven binary evolution in warped circumbinary discs: 3D moving-mesh hydrodynamics of eccentric and inclined binaries
new.summary: We present three-dimensional moving-mesh hydrodynamical simulations (\arepo{}) of equal-mass binaries in circumbinary discs, spanning binary eccentricity ($e = 0.0,\,0.3,\,0.6$) and inclination ($i = 0^\circ$--$60^\circ$), using a locally isothermal $\alpha$-disc ($H/r = \alpha_{\rm visc} = 0.1$) with fixed Keplerian orbits. Discs above the critical inclination $i_{\rm crit}(e)$, decreasing with $e$, drive their interiors near-polar, so eccentricity alone alters the outcome at fixed $i$. Discs reach polar alignment ten times faster than they align toward the binary plane, settling long before the binary's orbit responds. Alignment dictates how the disc acts on the binary. First, a disc tilting back toward the binary plane spends nearly all its torque reorienting the binary's orbit, whereas a disc driven polar redirects it into the orbit itself, which shrinks 10--20 times faster. Second, at $e = 0.6$ the turn to polar is a single transient reshaping the accretion flow, cavity and orbit, with accretion enhanced ($i = 45^\circ$) or suppressed ($i = 60^\circ$). Third, misalignment suppresses coplanar eccentricity pumping: the attractor at $e \approx 0.4$ survives only below $i \approx 15^\circ$, so misaligned binaries circularise and may enter the gravitational-wave regime less eccentric than coplanar models predict. Around a circular binary, the familiar $\approx 4.5$-orbit accretion modulation vanishes while the disc is strongly warped, returning as it realigns, a time-domain signature of misaligned massive black-hole binaries. Finally, observed polar discs around stellar binaries, such as HD~98800~BaBb's, are likely in their final state; intermediate misalignments reflect slower alignment toward the binary plane.

new.title: Newtonian I-Love-Q relations: An enthalpy-based approach
new.summary: We present a pedagogical introduction to the I-Love-Q relations within Newtonian gravity using an enthalpy-based formulation of stellar structure. Introducing the specific enthalpy converts Euler's equation into a first integral of hydrostatic equilibrium and recasts the equation of state as a relation between the mass density and the enthalpy. Together with Poisson's equation, these relations provide a unified description of spherical equilibrium and deformations induced by rotation and tides. We illustrate the formalism with polytropic equations of state and a relativistic free Fermi gas. In Newtonian gravity, slow uniform rotation and a weak tidal field excite the same linear quadrupolar response, yielding the exact identity $\bar I^{\,2}\bar Q/\bar\lambda\equiv1$ for the dimensionless (``bar'') observables---independently of the equation of state. This exact identity is distinguished from the approximate universality of the pairwise I-Love-Q relations, whose residual dependence on stellar structure is illustrated by the models considered in this work.

new.title: A Study of the 30 May 2026 Meteor Event Employing Data from Raspberry Boom Infrasound Sensors in the Boston Area
new.summary: Infrasound signals of one and a half cycles of a 0.4 Hz pressure pulse were detected from the 30 May 2026 meteor over Cape Cod Bay at several university and private Raspberry Boom sensors in the Greater Boston area. Our analyses of these signals demonstrate the ability to define directivity to the source of the event based on differences in the timing of the signals, to determine its identity and location by analysis of the relationship between event distance and sensor event timing, and event acoustical power by the infrasonic pressures measured at the sensor sites. The infrasound event is determined to be the atmospheric fireball blast at between 40 and 50 km in altitude with acoustic energy on the order of 5% to 14% of the total fireball energy.

new.title: Non-Axisymmetric Pillar Structures due to Embedded Stars in AGN Accretion Discs
new.summary: Gravitationally unstable outer regions of AGN discs may host in situ formation of massive stars whose heating produces localized vertical "pillars" on the disc surface, in the same region that emits the broad lines. Here we investigate the reverberation-mapping signatures that such pillars would produce. We compute velocity-delay maps $\Psi(\lambda, \tau)$, time-evolving emission-line spectra, and continuum reverberation lag spectra for these structures. We model each pillar as a 2D Gaussian perturbation to the disc height under lamp-post irradiation and weight the line response with Cloudy photoionization grids covering the major BLR lines. We show H$\alpha$, Mg II, and C IV as representative examples. A single pillar produces a localized hotspot in $\Psi$ and a clear "S-wave" pattern in the time-evolving spectrum that persists, though diluted, for $N \sim 100$ pillars. Emission-line fluxes are suppressed in shadows behind the pillars, but when normalized by H$\beta$ (or by the local continuum) the line-to-H$\beta$ ratios move in opposite directions: Mg II/H$\beta$ rises while C IV/H$\beta$ drops. This contrast distinguishes pillars from purely kinematic features that would modulate all lines by similar factors. Across scans of the pillar shape and lamp-post height, the pillar models produce an optical continuum reverberation lag spectrum of the observed magnitude. The once-per-orbit modulation grows with $\sin i$ from foreshortening, and at sufficiently high inclination the pillar's body geometrically self-occults its lamp-facing inner slope, adding a sharper near/far contrast. These signatures provide observational diagnostics for detecting in situ star formation in AGN discs through velocity-resolved reverberation mapping campaigns.

new.title: An Extra-nuclear Water Maser in NGC 1106 Likely Driven By An AGN Shock: Implications for Maser-based Black Hole Mass Measurements
new.summary: We present Very Large Array A-configuration ($0.13$'') 22 GHz spectral-line and continuum observations of the Swift-BAT detected Seyfert 2 galaxy, NGC 1106, aimed at localizing a water maser line offset from the host systemic velocity by 541 km s$^{-1}$. The 22 GHz continuum emission reveals a 352 pc extended structure within the nucleus of NGC 1106, and we spatially resolve the water maser emission to a compact region $\sim1$ kpc ($3.12$'') from the nucleus. Comparing our data with previous 22 GHz 1'' observations, we found that the water maser lies near the boundary of a radio extension aligned with the jet axis, likely arising from the interface between the active galactic nucleus (AGN) outflow and the host galaxy's ISM. To verify this, we compared the water maser in NGC 1106 to a known water maser in a star-forming region within the Milky Way, along with known extragalactic water masers associated with star formation and AGN driven outflows. Overall, we found that the maser position, velocity offset, flux density, and alignment with the jet axis are consistent with an origin at the interface between the AGN outflow and the host ISM. Our results have important implications for maser-based black hole mass measurements in which disk geometry is ambiguous. Since single-dish observations cannot spatially separate disk masers from outflow-driven masers, high-velocity maser features attributed to the accretion disk may also include contributions from kpc-scale shocks.

new.title: Image Morphology of Misaligned Magnetically Arrested Disks
new.summary: Horizon scale images probe the plasma dynamics and spacetime in the vicinity of accreting black holes. Interpreting these images requires models that connect image morphology to the structure of the underlying accretion flow. Disk misalignment is expected in many systems, yet most horizon scale image analyses assume that the emitting flow is aligned with the black hole spin. We investigate whether tilted accretion flows produce image features distinguishable from axisymmetric flows and whether their effects can be absorbed by changes in aligned model parameters. Using general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations of tilted magnetically arrested disks spanning black hole spins $a^*=-0.9375$ to $0.9375$ and initial disk tilts $0^\circ$ to $30^\circ$, we generate synthetic images and quantify their morphology through fits to an aligned, semi-analytic emission model. Using this approach, we show that high spin prograde models show little sensitivity to disk tilt, as the inner emitting flow aligns with the black hole spin. In contrast, retrograde tilted disks develop warped, non-axisymmetric inner structure that distorts the inner shadow and strongly alters image morphology. While the aligned semi-analytic model reproduces most prograde images well, retrograde tilted disk images are fit less accurately and yield biased inferred parameters, especially for spin. The image morphologies indicate that tilt affects horizon scale images only when misalignment survives into the near horizon emitting region, motivating image models that include disk tilt as an explicit degree of freedom when alignment is uncertain.

new.title: From Inspiral to Outburst: Modeling a Potential Luminous Red Nova from Betelgeuse
new.summary: Recent evidence suggests that Betelgeuse may host a stellar companion whose orbit will decay through tidal interactions, ultimately leading to engulfment and merger within the next several thousand years. If confirmed, this system could represent the nearest and best-characterized progenitor of a future luminous red nova (LRN). We investigate whether the shock-breakout and cooling emission preceding the LRN can be used to constrain the properties of the companion and its disruption within the stellar envelope. Using binary stellar evolution calculations, we evolve Betelgeuse with companions of $0.7$, $1.0$, and $2.0 M_\odot$ to the onset of common envelope evolution (CEE). We then perform one-dimensional radiation-hydrodynamic simulations that follow companion disruption, energy deposition, and shock propagation through the envelope. We find that the peak luminosity increases systematically with companion mass, from $2.44\times10^{41}$ to $6.17\times10^{41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ across the $0.7$-$2.0 M_\odot$ models, while the duration increases more modestly from $1.48$ to $1.99$ days and attains apparent magnitudes brighter than Venus as viewed from Earth. Tidal disruption contributes both kinetic energy and mass to the envelope, linking the companion's structure and mass to the energetics of the shock-heated ejecta. The monotonic luminosity sequence demonstrates that the early breakout emission can retain direct information about the engulfed companion. The interaction ejects $6.15$-$11.19 M_\odot$ of hydrogen-rich material, substantially modifying both the envelope structure and circumstellar environment prior to core collapse.

new.title: Collapsars Are Not Heavy $r$-Process Factories
new.summary: Collapsar disks are proposed sources of $r$-process elements, but neutron-rich disk ejecta require gas to be both neutronized in the disk and ejected before accretion. The magnetic field that enables ejection also thickens the disk and accelerates the inflow, lowering both the density and the time available for weak processing. To compute the resulting neutronization, we evolve the electron fraction of the inflowing gas, adopting at each radius the temperature that maximizes the net neutronization rate for the local density and instantaneous composition. This yields a lower limit on $Y_{\rm e}$ that is independent of the disk's thermal history. We adopt an optimistic unbinding radius of $R_{\rm unb}=10\,r_g$ for all magnetic fluxes capable of launching outflows. Combining this ejection condition with favorable assumptions of low black hole mass, ejection of midplane gas, and the upper end of the $\gamma$-ray burst (GRB) engine-power scale, which limits the accretion rate to $\dot M_{\rm BH}\lesssim0.4\,M_\odot\,{\rm s}^{-1}$, gives a fiducial lower bound $Y_{\rm e}\gtrsim0.33$, above the characteristic $Y_{\rm e}\approx 0.25$ threshold for heavy $r$-process production. Stronger magnetic flux, toward which jet-launching engines evolve, raises the lower bound to $Y_{\rm e}\gtrsim0.49$. We conclude that collapsar disk outflows cannot supply the heavy $r$-process yields invoked for a dominant enrichment channel. Only engines with unusually high accretion rates, potentially including exceptionally luminous GRBs, such as GRB 221009A, and direct-horizon collapsars, may produce heavy $r$-process ejecta.

new.title: Prospects of Detecting Cosmological Domain Walls in the Cosmic Microwave Background
new.summary: Topological defects are a generic prediction of field theories with spontaneously broken symmetries, and domain walls, the two-dimensional defects left by a broken discrete symmetry, are among the simplest. We study the imprint of dark, purely gravitationally interacting domain walls on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), in the regime where a low symmetry-breaking scale $\eta$ allows the walls to evade the Zel'dovich overclosure bound while remaining cosmologically relevant. The relativistic repulsion of matter by a planar wall carves out an evacuated void bounded by an overdense shell, and we compute the resulting photon deflection field analytically for walls both aligned with and arbitrarily inclined to the line of sight. The deflection stamps coherent, strongly non-Gaussian distortions onto the temperature sky, with a characteristic two-peak structure set by the relativistic displacement scale and an inclination dependence that vanishes for face-on walls. Because these signatures are localised and anisotropic, they are poorly captured by two-point statistics; we therefore analyse them with a curvelet/wavelet decomposition matched to the wall's geometry, and with simulation-based inference, training a Neural Posterior Estimator (NPE) to recover the scattering redshift $z$, energy scale $\eta$, and inclination $\theta$, and a Neural Ratio Estimator (NRE) to evaluate the likelihood-ratio test statistic for limit-setting. Casting these methods as sensitivity forecasts for a South Pole Telescope-like (SPT) survey, we find that the curvelet and wavelet statistical thresholds populate a common $\eta \sim 10-100$ MeV band over the accessible redshift range. The neural-ratio sensitivity curve, which exploits the full map morphology, reaches a factor 1.3-1.9 lower in $\eta$ at $z \gtrsim 20$, or $\sim 2-7$ in the wall tension, landing essentially on the per-resolution-element noise floor.

new.title: FastSpec: Fast and versatile stellar spectrum synthesis code
new.summary: Modelling data from modern spectroscopic surveys and time-resolved spectropolarimetric observations requires stellar synthetic spectra to be computed rapidly over wide wavelength ranges from line lists that increasingly reach hundreds of millions of transitions. Spectropolarimetric analyses of magnetically active stars additionally demand a solution of the polarised radiative transfer problem. We present FastSpec, a new LTE spectrum synthesis code designed around two goals: increased raw computational speed and broad astrophysical applicability, including the calculation of the full Stokes vector in the presence of a magnetic field. FastSpec computes emergent intensity and flux spectra from plane-parallel and spherical model atmospheres. Chemical and ionisation equilibrium is obtained from the updated SME equation-of-state package, continuum opacities follow the ATLAS family of routines, hydrogen bound-bound and bound-free absorption uses the occupation-probability formalism, and line absorption is evaluated with fast table-based Voigt and Faraday-Voigt profile algorithms. The transfer equation is integrated with DELO-Bezier formal solvers in both scalar and Stokes-vector form. Speed is achieved through aggressive OpenMP parallelisation, adaptive per-line wavelength windowing, and a memory-capped block-processing scheme that lets arbitrarily large line lists be handled within a user-defined RAM budget. The code synthesises spectra thousands of Å wide from line lists of $10^8$ molecular and atomic transitions in under a minute on a modern multi-core laptop while reproducing benchmark calculations from established codes. FastSpec combines the physical completeness of classical model atmosphere and spectrum synthesis codes with the speed required by large surveys and the polarised transfer needed for stellar magnetism studies into a single portable package.

new.title: The Galactic Center Reference Frame: A 30-Year Solution
new.summary: Stellar orbits probe the metric of and mass around the Sgr A* massive black hole. To enable study of the black hole, the surrounding mass, and tests of gravity, a precise reference frame must be established and maintained. We present an updated stellar maser-based reference frame for the inner parsec of the Galactic Center, referenced to the radio continuum of Sgr A*. This work synthesizes 30 years of astrometric observations of 15 SiO stellar masers and the Sgr A* continuum at 43 GHz. The uncertainty in the mean offset of the maser ensemble from Sgr A* is 0.08 mas in the current epoch and will decay to 0.10 mas by 2030. At a distance of 8.2 kpc, these correspond to position uncertainties of 0.6 AU and 0.8 AU, respectively, which is similar to or smaller than the stellar SiO-emitting region. The mean maser proper motion uncertainties are 0.05 mas yr$^{-1}$ in RA and 0.08 mas yr$^{-1}$ in Dec, corresponding to 1.8 km s$^{-1}$ and 3.2 km s$^{-1}$. The reference frame stability between IR and maser astrometry is 10~$\mu$as yr$^{-1}$ (0.40 km s$^{-1}$) in RA and 15 $\mu$as yr$^{-1}$ (0.57 km s$^{-1}$) in Dec. The masers show substantial variability in flux density and velocity structure, most notably IRS~7, which shows a 30-fold brightening in a blueshifted component since 2022. This variability may set a floor on future astrometry improvements and especially measurements of radial acceleration.

new.title: AMICO galaxy clusters in KiDS-1000: Cosmological constraints from the two-point correlation function
new.summary: In this paper we study the clustering properties of an optically identified photometric galaxy cluster catalogue from KiDS-1000. The sample was identified by the AMICO algorithm and consists of 9049 clusters with $S/N\geq3.5$, in the redshift range $0.1\leq z<0.8$, spread over an effective area of 838.78 deg$^2$. Clusters are selected according to their observed intrinsic richness, with thresholds of $\lambda^*{obs}\geq 20,25,30$ within $0.10\leq z<0.30$, $0.30\leq z<0.45$ and $0.45\leq z<0.80$, respectively. We measure the multipoles of the two-point correlation function over different ranges of scales from 5 $h^{-1}$ Mpc to 150 $h^{-1}$ Mpc. We model the clustering signal in the context of the $\Lambda$CDM cosmology, accounting for the main observational effects, such RSDs and photo-$z$ uncertainties. The effective bias of the cluster sample is estimated via a mass-richness scaling relation. For the MCMC analysis, we adopt Gaussian priors on the parameters of the mass-richness scaling relation, and broad, uniform priors to derive cosmological constraints on the cold matter density parameter, the power spectrum amplitude and the structure growth parameter, $S_8\equiv\sigma_8 \sqrt{\Omega{m}/0.3}$. Specifically, we find $\Omega_{m}=0.24^{+0.02}{-0.02}$ and $\sigma_8=0.86^{+0.13}{-0.10}$ representing an improvement in precision over both the 2D and 3D AMICO clustering analyses performed on the previous KiDS data release. Moreover, we obtain $S_8=0.77^{+0.10}_{-0.08}$ in $1\sigma$ agreement with the AMICO KiDS-1000 number counts constraints estimated from the same catalogue, as well as with some results from external early- and late-Universe data sets. Our work strengthens the potential of cluster clustering as a complementary and competitive probe, to be included and further developed with the final KiDS-Legacy data release, and in other future Stage-IV photometric redshift surveys.

new.title: The Impact of Orbital Data Centers on the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory
new.summary: As the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory begins its Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), satellite operators are racing to launch Orbital Data Center (ODC) satellites into low-Earth orbit. We present an impact assessment of a simulated $\sim$1 million ODC satellite constellation, arranged per recent filings across two low-Earth and two Sun-synchronous orbit regimes, on one year of Rubin Observatory LSST observations. Our six-stage sequential pipeline combines orbit propagation, field-of-view matching, observer-frame geometry, brightness modeling, surface-brightness calculations, and pixel-loss estimates. We find that on a given night, up to 80% of LSST pointings would contain at least one illuminated ODC satellite streak, depending on the time of year. The yearly average of contaminated exposures is closer to 20%, due to seasonal visibility variations and bright satellite streaks being most prominent near twilight. Sun-synchronous ODCs disproportionately contaminate due to preferential illumination geometry. The ODC satellite brightness distribution is multi-modal, where solar panel specular reflection can appear as bright as 2-4 AB mag ($\mu_g \approx 9-11$ mag arcsec$^{-2}$), while diffuse reflections more typically reach 6 AB mag ($\mu_g \approx 13-14$ mag arcsec$^{-2}$). Even at 10% deployment, the constellation would still produce widespread visible streak contamination throughout the year. ODC satellites would also drastically increase sky brightness -- by more than 1000% near twilight with no Moon. Launching and operating ODC satellites at this scale would significantly harm LSST science, including typical 5-10% nightly mean pixel losses near twilight, even if multiple mitigation strategies are implemented.

new.title: Demographics of Close-In TESS Exoplanets Orbiting FGK Main-sequence Stars II. Spectral-Type Dependence and the Neptunian Landscape
new.summary: Understanding how planetary demographics depend on host star properties is essential for constraining planet formation and evolution theories. In this paper, we analyse close-in 0.5-16 d planet occurrence rates from the TESS Science Processing Operations Center (SPOC) full-frame image data for individual F-, G-, and K-type main-sequence stellar samples. Integrated over $0.5 < P < 16$ d and $2 < R_\mathrm{p} < 20\,R_\oplus$, the occurrence rates are $12.1^{+3.0}_{-2.3}$, $10.2^{+1.2}_{-1.0}$, and $13.1^{+1.4}_{-1.2}$ planets per 100 stars for F-, G-, and K-type hosts, consistent with each other at $1\sigma$, so any spectral-type dependence is localized rather than global. For transiting hot Jupiters, we measure $0.30^{+0.04}_{-0.03}$, $0.50\pm0.03$, and $0.67^{+0.08}_{-0.07}$ per cent, with the rate peaking at K type; the latter being the first such measurement for K-type hosts. Modelling the Neptunian desert directly in occurrence-rate space, we find that the desert extends to longer orbital periods around hotter stars. Integrating over the desert interior gives $0.069^{+0.045}_{-0.011}$, $0.093^{+0.046}_{-0.022}$, and $0.150^{+0.033}_{-0.026}$ planets per 100 stars, implying about one close-in planet in a hundred lies inside the desert, and the desert is roughly twice as populated around K- as around F-type hosts. A rigorous Bayesian model comparison for the $6$-$8\,R_\oplus$ strip indicates that a distinct Neptunian ridge is not required to explain the measurements.

new.title: Cluster connectivity in DES Y3 data: impact on galaxy properties
new.summary: Connectivity, namely the number of cosmic filaments reaching out of groups or clusters, has recently emerged as an informative way to quantify environment. With the advent of wide-area photometric surveys, it becomes possible to measure connectivity on a statistically significant sample of clusters. In this work, we extract the cosmic web from the DES Y3 photometric data and measure the connectivity around clusters from several public catalogs up to $z < 1$. Cosmic filaments are extracted in 2D with DisPerSE (the parametrization of which is calibrated on simulations) in tomographic slices of fixed comoving thickness of 220 Mpc, with a constant sampling across the redshift range ($\sim 0.1$ galaxies Mpc$^{-2}$). We first recover the well-established trend that cluster connectivity increases with cluster mass at all redshifts. We then investigate the properties of cluster member galaxies and find that, at fixed mass, clusters with a higher fraction of red (elliptical) galaxies are more strongly connected to the cosmic web. Furthermore, by examining the radial profiles of the red and elliptical galaxy fractions, we obtain hints that galaxy populations may undergo pre-processing within filamentary structures before being accreted into clusters. Overall, we demonstrate that despite photometric redshift uncertainties and projection effects, our method allows for the quantification of the cosmic web environment around clusters in broad-band photometric surveys. This work is consistent with results based on the Euclid Quick Release 1 (Q1). We plan to publicly release the cluster connectivity catalog as well as the cosmic filament catalog.

new.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks vs U-Net: Application to thermal dust emission recovery in the microwave
new.summary: Galactic thermal dust emission is the dominant foreground contaminant of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) at frequencies above 100 GHz, and its accurate separation is essential for current and future CMB experiments. Deep learning methods, in particular convolutional architectures such as the U-Net, have demonstrated strong performance for CMB component separation, but typically operate as purely data-driven models with no explicit enforcement of the physical laws governing the emission they reconstruct. In this work, we present a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) that embeds the Modified Black Body (MBB) spectral model as a hard, differentiable architectural constraint, and we compare it against a standard U-Net baseline trained under an identical pipeline. Both architectures are trained on realistic simulated Planck HFI patches at four frequencies (143, 217, 353 and 545 GHz) and evaluated on a shared validation set as well as on three independent Galactic dust realizations from the PySM phenomenological dust models named D4, D7 and D10. We find that both networks achieve comparable reconstruction quality across all evaluated datasets, with a Structural Similarity Index Measure consistently above 0.96 and a fitted angular power-spectrum spectral index that agrees with the input to within 1% in every region. Embedding the physical constraint in the PINN does not measurably degrade reconstruction accuracy relative to the unconstrained U-Net, while additionally guaranteeing that every predicted output corresponds to a thermodynamically admissible physical configuration. These results establish the physics-informed formulation as a viable methodological alternative for dust component separation, providing physical interpretability without a trade-off in reconstruction fidelity.

new.title: Best Bulk Bennu (B3): Elemental compositions of aggregate samples from asteroid Bennu
new.summary: Ivuna-type (CI) carbonaceous chondrites have long served as proxies for the bulk Solar System composition due to their close agreement with solar photospheric abundances and enrichment in volatile elements relative to other chondrite classes. However, CI chondrites have been subject to terrestrial alteration, which may have modified their original mineralogies and redistributed aqueously mobile elements. NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission delivered pristine material from the carbonaceous asteroid Bennu, and initial analyses revealed close compositional similarities with CI chondrites. This provides a valuable opportunity to refine estimates of the bulk Solar System composition. We report concentrations of 63 elements in aggregate (bulk, unsorted) Bennu material (representing a combined mass of ~8 g) analyzed across four laboratories. Within analytical uncertainties, we find no statistically significant differences among aliquots of two aggregate samples that were homogenized into powders, or among subsamples (including two previously reported) of a non-homogenized aggregate sample. Nor do we find measurable variations among sample masses ranging from tens of milligrams to several grams. These findings indicate that the material returned from Bennu is well mixed at the aggregate scale. Combining all of the data, we derive an average bulk elemental composition that we term Best Bulk Bennu (B3). Comparison of B3 with an average CI chondrite composition shows excellent agreement within analytical uncertainties, confirming that terrestrial alteration of CI chondrites is effectively isochemical for non-highly volatile elements. B3 and the CI chondrite average composition compare similarly to solar photospheric composition. Thus, CI meteorites and returned samples of carbonaceous asteroids are the best available materials for estimating the bulk Solar System composition of non-highly volatile elements.

new.title: Listening to the Standard Candles: A Survey-Scale Search for Phase-Coded Beacons in Cepheids, RR~Lyrae and $β$~Cephei Stars
new.summary: Learned et al. (2008) proposed that a civilization could use Cepheids and RR Lyrae stars, the most closely watched clocks in astronomy, as beacons, firing pulsations early with a particle beam to write a message into the timing residuals. The one search to date examined a single Kepler star. We describe Star SETI, an automated pipeline that selects Cepheids, RR Lyrae and $\beta$ Cephei stars from Gaia DR3, measures per-cycle (TESS, Kepler) or block-averaged (ASAS-SN, ZTF) observed-minus-computed timing residuals, tests them for non-white structure, decodes them as a bit stream under the cumulative (``staircase'') modulation of a one-sided trigger, and matches the words to catalogs of recognizable sequences. A resonant antineutrino beam grazing the base of the driving zone needs hundreds to tens of thousands of times less power than a central beam, and driving an RR Lyrae star takes most of its light. Injections into real light curves show that only RR Lyrae stars are detectable near the amplitude that Learned et al. proposed, with half of the codes recovered at 0.2--0.4 per cent of a period per bit in TESS; the ground-based surveys detect only codes held for tens of cycles per bit and decode none. We time 97,725 light curves of 77,596 stars and vet 38,230 timing anomalies; 6823 have timing structure that the vetting cannot attribute to a known cause, all but eight of them on block-averaged timing to which only part of the vetting applies. The highest-ranked are non-radial modes in first-overtone RR Lyrae stars, Blazhko modulation and mode beating in $\beta$ Cephei stars, and no decoded word survives a false-discovery correction. We find no beacon. That bounds only beacons: a perfectly compressed message is indistinguishable from noise, so a civilization communicating efficiently rather than advertising could leave residuals that pass all of our tests, in stars that we cannot single out.

new.title: Semi-Analytic Predictions for Strong-Lensing Perturbers in Cold and Self-Interacting Dark Matter
new.summary: Strong gravitational lensing is sensitive to the abundance and internal structure of dark matter halos, providing a probe of gravothermal evolution in self-interacting dark matter (SIDM). We combine semi-analytic cold dark matter (CDM) subhalo histories with a model for gravothermal evolution in SIDM to generate CDM and SIDM subhalo populations across SIDM parameter space. We predict their projected enclosed masses and deflection-based projected density slopes and compare them with three perturbers inferred through gravitational imaging in PJ011646, SDSS J0946+1006, and JVAS B1938+666. For SIDM model parameters $\sigma_0/m_\chi=147.1$ cm$^2$/g and $w=120$ km/s, SIDM subhalos reproduce all three perturbers more often than CDM subhalos. For PJ011646, we find ~0.6 cored SIDM subhalos per host matching the perturber, compared with ~0.002 in CDM, while core-collapsed subhalos are too steep. For SDSS J0946+1006, we find ~3 core-collapsed and ~0.004 cored SIDM subhalos per host, compared with none in 900 CDM realizations, although baryons, neglected here, may matter for such massive subhalos. For "detection V" in JVAS B1938+666, we find ~220 core-collapsed and ~20 cored SIDM subhalos per host within the $2\sigma$ posterior region, compared with ~0.2 in CDM; the CDM candidates require exceptionally early accretion, at median redshift $z\sim13$. Simultaneously reproducing all three perturbers requires $w\gtrsim10^2$ km/s, so that the massive (~$5.6\times10^{10}M_\odot$) progenitors of SDSS J0946+1006 candidates can collapse, and is achieved for $\sigma_0/m_\chi\gtrsim10^2$ cm$^2$/g in the parameter sets studied. Our results show how semi-analytic models can quantify how often subhalos reproduce individual perturbers in different dark matter models, and our modular framework can be readily updated as models of tidal stripping and late-stage gravothermal evolution in SIDM improve. (abridged)

new.title: Discovery of activity on Main Belt Asteroid 6993 (1995 BJ4)
new.summary: We report the discovery of activity on asteroid 6993 (1995 BJ4) in the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) alert stream data on UT 2026 August 5, with the help of machine learning. Visible activity can be seen as early as UT 2026 June 25. Activity on this outer-main belt object is likely not primarily driven by rotational instability, but rather is consistent with an impact event or sublimation based on several arguments. If this activity is sublimation driven, 6993 would be the largest known main belt comet (11.85 km), with the largest perihelion distance (2.853 au) and an unusually high geometric albedo of 0.166 $\pm$ 0.030. Asteroid 6993 should be monitored as it approaches perihelion in 2027 January to distinguish between activity mechanisms and understand its potential volatile inventory.

new.title: The SDSS-V Local Volume Mapper (LVM): Technical Overview
new.summary: The Sloan Digital Sky Survey V (SDSS-V) Local Volume Mapper (LVM) is an ultra-wide integral field spectroscopic survey of the Milky Way, the Magellanic Clouds, and a sample of galaxies in the local volume. The LVM spatially resolved spectroscopy covers the bulk of the optical range (3600-9800 A) at medium spectral-resolution (R = 2200-5500), and maps the disks of these galaxies at high physical spatial resolution (< 1 pc in the MW and ~10 pc in the Magellanic Clouds). Observations are carried out with the LVM Instrument (LVM-I), a custom-built robotic telescope, instrument, and facility located at Las Campanas Observatory (LCO) in Chile. In this article we present a technical overview of the LVM project. We describe the hardware, the survey observing strategy, and the details of how science and calibration observations are carried out. We provide a high-level overview of the survey data flow, including the reduction and calibration of the LVM spectra, and the production of the main data products that are released by the project. We also present an assessment of the LVM data quality and instrumental stability based on science observations. The main goal of this article is to serve as a primer for LVM users, providing the technical information required for the adequate analysis, modeling, and interpretation of the LVM data.

new.title: Tilt, warp, and dissipation flare in hydrodynamic disks around kicked compact objects
new.summary: We study the dynamical response of a hydrodynamic disk to an impulsive kick imparted to a central massive object, focusing on the global properties of the material that remains gravitationally bound. We construct a simple analytic model and show that the bound material can acquire a significant tilt---or even a retrograde rotation---if the kick is directed close to the disk midplane. We perform 3D numerical simulations and show that (1) the bound material relaxes to a torus-like circularized flow of which total mass and angular momentum is in fair agreement with the analytic estimate, and (2) in spite of nonlinear hydrodynamic effects, a highly tilted or retrograde disk can be sufficiently formed. The simulations additionally reveal a transient warp in the kicked disk, suggesting a kick as a formation mechanism of tilted or warped disks around compact objects. About 10% of the kinetic energy the bound material acquired from the kick is converted to the internal energy, while the exact conversion efficiency depends on the kick angle and the initial surface mass density profile. The luminosity of this kick-driven dissipation flare can reach $\sim 10^{43}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ for strong kicks ($V_{\rm kick} \sim 1000$km/s). We discuss the implications of our results for recoiling supermassive black holes, recoiled stellar-mass black holes in the disks of active galactic nuclei, and natal kicks on compact objects.

new.title: The Impact of Inclination, Redshift, and Mass Ratio Selection on Cosmological Constraints from Bright Sirens Beyond Conventional Fisher Approximations
new.summary: Future generations of gravitational-wave observatories are projected to detect up to thousands bright siren events within a decade of operation. However, the precision of these cosmological forecasts depends heavily on the astrophysical assumptions embedded within the simulation pipelines. In this work, we systematically investigate the impact of variations in the binary mass ratio ($q$), the maximum observable inclination angle ($\iota_{\max}$), and the maximum redshift ($z_{\max}$) on the constraints of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) and the matter density parameter ($\Omega_m$). We perform our analyses based on the GWDALI framework, the GW Doublet Approximation, and the phenomenological waveform approximant IMRPhenomD. By adopting sets of non-spinning binary neutron star populations we explore the impact of astrophysical parameters on the constraints of cosmological parameters. Our results reveal a clear dichotomy in the observational requirements: while the statistical uncertainty on $H_0$ falls below the falls below approximately $1.3\%$ level for $N \ge 400$ events and drops under $0.9\%$ once $N \ge 800$, a deep-redshift catalog ($z_{\max} \ge 1.0$) is strictly required to effectively break parameter degeneracies and constrain the global geometry through $\Omega_m$. Furthermore, expanding the maximum inclination cutoff from the conservative $20^{\circ}$ up to $40^{\circ}$ substantially mitigates the correlation between distance and inclination.

new.title: OGLE-2015-BLG-1395Lb: A Cold Sub-Saturn Mass Planet Orbiting an M Dwarf
new.summary: We present an analysis of the high-magnification microlensing event OGLE-2015-BLG-1395 and report the discovery of a sub-Saturn mass companion to the lens. Photometric coverage of the planetary anomaly in the light curve was obtained from the University of Tasmania's Harlingten 1.27m telescope. Additional data were obtained following the peak from several other observatories, allowing photometric calibration and color measurement of the source. Fits to the light curve reveal a companion with mass ratio of q = 0.00062 +/- 0.00007 and two degenerate solutions for the projected separation, s = 1.7 +/-0.1 or 0.59 +/-0.04 Einstein ring radii. Source and lens parameters are further constrained by Subaru and Keck adaptive optics (AO) imaging in 2016. Finite source effects and AO flux constraints allow us to determine the planet and host star parameters to better than a factor of 2. The system is an ~0.2 Jupiter-mass planet orbiting an ~0.25 solar mass (early-mid M-dwarf) main-sequence star in the Galactic disk, at a distance of ~2 kpc. The two degenerate solutions from the light curve both place the planet beyond the snow line. As a cold sub-Saturn around an M dwarf, OGLE-2015-BLG-1395Lb is in possible conflict with core accretion theory. Spitzer photometry from the time of the event is consistent with this conclusion, although highly uncertain due to faintness and crowding. The inferred relative proper motion of 9.4 mas/yr is consistent with a source star in the bulge and a lens in the disk, and predicts that the source and lens could be resolved a decade after the event.

new.title: A Unified Model for Radioactive Signatures and Source Identifiability in Neutron Star Mergers
new.summary: Late light curves of neutron star mergers can contain substantial fission power while remaining compatible with different radioactive inventories. We develop a unified source attribution model in which a common bounded response formulation links nuclear heating, radiation transport and isotope identification. Within particle dependent deposition and gray photon escape, matched luminosity comparisons show how long alpha and fission responses become aligned. Explicit competing inventories then reproduce a light curve with a substantial $^{254}$Cf contribution, with smooth evolution of the beta luminosity response providing an important source of compensation. We derive optimization certificates and collective likelihood bounds that quantify the resulting limits on identification under specified source and ejecta constraints. We also introduce an energy conserving model with two radiation frequency groups to resolve the information carried by color at fixed total luminosity precision. Its exact response modes identify the source adjustments that absorb color contrast, while a residual color floor characterizes the contrast retained by the permitted family. Late observations of AT~2023vfi with the James Webb and Hubble Space Telescopes provide an observational benchmark: the reference and retained alternatives predict bolometric declines about 1.5 quoted uncertainties shallower than the reconstruction, while differences between inventories containing and excluding $^{254}$Cf remain within the reported decline uncertainty. The unified model provides a quantitative basis for connecting nucleosynthesis predictions, gravitational wave constraints and the temporal and spectral information in merger observations to radioactive source attribution.

new.title: FacilityAudit-Agent: Beyond Mention-as-Usage for Fine-Grained Facility Contribution Attribution in Astrophysics Publications
new.summary: Observatory bibliographies increasingly need to determine not only whether a facility is named in a paper, but how its data support the scientific argument. We frame this need as semantic contribution attribution on a six-level scale (L0-L5), from non-use and mention-only cases to auxiliary, major, and exclusive data support. We present FacilityAudit-Agent, a framework that builds a page-bounded outline of each PDF, enriches sections with roles and facility mentions, and uses a tool-calling large language model (LLM) to fetch text on demand. Evidence from the sections is combined through an explicit decision tree and a coverage-calibrated confidence score, with uncertain cases routed to human review. The framework supports both single-facility and inventory audits and transfers to new facilities without retraining. On a test set of 39,358 human-annotated paper-facility pairs, FacilityAudit-Agent achieves 89.1% accuracy and 79.8% macro-F1 in single_audit mode, outperforming the other three baselines by 5.8, 8.3, and 12.1 accuracy points, respectively, with the clearest gains at L2 and L5. In inventory_audit mode, it also leads in facility listing and in level assignment among listed pairs. Ablations show multi-hop reading and tree indexing matter most for L3-L5. FacilityAudit-Agent has been deployed at the National Astronomical Data Center, where it is responsible for processing publications related to LAMOST, FAST, and EP.

new.title: SMMAN Studies of AGN Variability. I. Long-term Spectral Evolution and a Candidate $\sim1000$-day Quasi-periodic Modulation in 4C+72.28
new.summary: The SMMAN project has carried out nine years of radio flux monitoring in the C and K bands of the blazar 4C+72.28. The two bands show markedly different secular evolution, with a substantially stronger K-band decline producing a gradual decrease in the C-K spectral index. After accounting for this secular evolution, multiple timing diagnostics reveal a candidate quasi-periodic modulation with a characteristic timescale of $\sim1000$ d, most clearly in the C band. The C-band GLSP peak reaches a local significance of $3.29\sigma$, while its global significance remains modest at $\sim2\sigma$ and the monitoring baseline covers only about three cycles. Independent and joint MCMC fits support a phenomenological decomposition for both bands into a long-term linear trend and a recurrent component. Under the shared-period assumption, the joint fit returns a characteristic timescale of approximately 1027 d and a similar fractional recurrent amplitudes of $\simeq5.45\%$. Information-criterion comparisons favor the combined linear-plus-sinusoidal model in both bands. Cross-correlation analysis shows a nominal K-leading offset in the original light curves but a centroid consistent with zero lag after detrending, although the lag distributions overlap substantially. These results are consistent with a common recurrent modulation superposed on slower frequency-dependent jet evolution. Geometrical Doppler-factor modulation provides one plausible interpretation, although intrinsic and opacity-related processes cannot be excluded.

new.title: Galaxy Luminosity Functions at z~7-10 from Four Years of JWST Observations
new.summary: We present galaxy luminosity functions at $z\approx 7.4$ and 10 based on a comprehensive search for candidate galaxies at $6.4\lesssim z\lesssim11.3$ in JWST's public NIRCam data four years after its operation. Our work utilises nine fields covering $\sim$1,045~arcmin$^2$ in total, including seven blank fields and two galaxy cluster fields. Using the dropout technique, we selected 3,733 dropouts from the F090W passband and 2,396 dropouts from the F115W passband, which constitute the largest samples of candidate galaxies at $z\approx 7.4$ and $z\approx 10$ to date. Among these objects, 338 F090W-dropouts and 99 F115W-dropouts already have secure redshifts from JWST NIRSpec spectroscopy over four years, which we use to form two large spectroscopic subsamples to assess the magnitude-dependent contamination rates of their parent dropout samples. Our luminosity functions are based on the results after statistically correcting for both incompleteness and contamination. We find that the luminosity function at $z\approx 7.4$ can be well described by a conventional Schechter function but with a faint-end slope of $\alpha=-1.70\pm0.16$ that is significantly shallower than most of the previous studies at $z\approx 7$--8. To verify this result, more imaging and spectroscopy at $\sim$30~mag will be needed. The luminosity function at $z\approx 10$, on the other hand, can hardly be fitted by a Schechter function but is more consistent with a power law in the form of $\Phi(M)\propto 10^{-0.4(\beta+1)M}$, with the best-fit slope of $\beta=-2.36\pm0.16$. While such a behavior is largely driven by the high number densities at $M_{\rm UV}\lesssim -21.8$~mag, it is supported by the currently existing spectroscopic confirmations. Further spectroscopy at the bright end($\lesssim 26$~mag) will be needed to strengthen this result.

We here discuss what we presently know about particle acceleration in radio galaxies, focusing particularly on the nearest such object, Centaurus A.

new.title: A Framework for Analysing Nebular-Phase JWST Supernova Spectra with Application to Type Ic SN 2024aecx
new.summary: We analyse what physical quantities of SN ejecta can be obtained from a single epoch of nebular JWST spectroscopy. We provide an analytical framework, which together with a grid of helium star \texttt{SUMO} spectral synthesis models allows the determination of these quantities for any stripped-envelope SN. Using the framework, we derive critical electron densities for major emission lines, finding values in the range $10^5-10^6$ cm$^{-3}$. This means formation under close to LTE conditions for 200 -- 300 days. We obtain ionisation fractions of Ni and Co, as well as the temperature and filling factor of the Fe/He zone, the $^{56}$Ni and stable nickel masses, the Ni/Fe ratio, and the optical depths $\tau_{\mathrm{[Ni\,II]\, 6.636 \mu m}}$ and $\tau_{\mathrm{[Co\,II]\, 10.52 \mu m}}$. Besides these constraints from iron group elements, one can also obtain the filling factor of the carbon burning (O/Ne/Mg) zone from [Ne II] 12.81 $\mu$m, and the masses of Ar II and Cl I. We apply our methodology to a publicly available JWST spectrum of Type Ic SN 2024aecx. We find that this SN produced a chlorine mass of $M_{\mathrm{Cl\, I}} \simeq M_{\mathrm{Cl}} = 5.1^{+2.0}_{-1.6}\times 10^{-4}$ $M_{\odot}$, a factor a few larger than expected from stellar evolution modeling. Furthermore, we find that the SN experienced an unexpectedly small 'Ni-bubble' effect, with $\rho_{\mathrm{FeHe}} = 2.5^{+0.7}_{-0.4} \times 10^{-15}$ g cm$^{-3}$ (or an expansion factor of 1 -- 3 for the Ni-bubble, depending on the adopted model) at 167d for the silicon burning material. We also determine $M_{\mathrm{Ar\, II}} = 4.9^{+2.2}_{-1.5} \times 10^{-4}$ $M_{\odot}$, which from ionisation fractions in our NLTE models yields a best estimate of $M_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 1.1 \pm 0.4 \times 10^{-3}$ $M_{\odot}$.

new.title: Differential and integral scaling laws of the mass density of molecular clouds
new.summary: In this work we investigate the mass density - size scaling law in molecular clouds (MCs). This relation reflects the fractal nature of MCs and plays a key role for understanding the physics, structure and evolution of these objects. We make use of the notion "ensemble of MCs", introduced in our previous work (Donkov, Veltchev \& Klessen, 2017), in which all MCs with the same probability density function (PDF) of mass density and effective size are represented by an abstract spherical cloud with the same PDF and size. In this spirit, the model is built on the base of abstract scales of the clouds' substructures (which are simply the radii of the spherical object). We consider two forms of the mass density - size scaling law: differential and integral, which in turn reveal the local and the global fractal clouds' structure. Both scaling functions are characterized by their scaling exponents, which can be explicitly expressed by the PDF of mass density, in the general case. Moreover, we derive a first order linear differential equation connecting the two scaling exponents and obtain its exact solution. As examples we apply this abstract construction to two PDFs: the so called power-law tail and the log-normal. Both have great importance for MC structure and evolution, as the latter corresponds to the earlier stages of clouds' evolution, when supersonic turbulence dominates the physical processes, while the former describes the latest stages of evolution, when star-formation takes place. The obtained results for the scaling exponents in both examples are qualitatively and numerically consistent with respective observations and simulations of MCs.

new.title: Probing Red Giant Interiors with g-Dominated Mixed Modes II: The Cases of KIC 6117517, KIC 9475697, KIC 10123207 and KIC 10200377
new.summary: Building on Paper~I, which constrained core overshooting to $f_{\rm ov} < 0.01$ for $M < 1.4\,M_{\odot}$ and found $\alpha_{\rm MLT} \simeq 2.0$ for metal-rich red giants, we extend this analysis to four lower-mass \textit{Kepler} red giants spanning a broad metallicity range: KIC~6117517, KIC~9475697, KIC~10123207, and KIC~10200377. Two complementary model grids are constructed: Grid~A fixes $\alpha_{\rm MLT} = 2.0$ while varying metallicity; Grid~B adopts spectroscopic metallicities with $\alpha_{\rm MLT}$ as a free parameter. Grid~A successfully reproduces both asteroseismic and spectroscopic constraints for the metal-rich targets (KIC~6117517 and KIC~9475697), confirming $\alpha_{\rm MLT} = 2.0$ for metal-rich red giants. For the metal-poor targets (KIC~10123207 and KIC~10200377), Grid~B yields larger mixing-length parameters of $\alpha_{\rm MLT} \approx 2.16$--$2.18$. Although only four stars are analyzed with unequal sensitivity to $\alpha_{\rm MLT}$, these results suggest a tentative increase in convective efficiency toward lower metallicity, consistent with 3D hydrodynamical simulations but opposite to some 1D empirical calibrations. The best-fitting overshooting parameters ($f_{\rm ov} = 0.006$--$0.007$) independently support the Paper~I constraint and are consistent with a mass-dependent overshooting relation. The parameter uncertainties reach $0.6$--$2.5\%$ in mass, $0.2$--$0.9\%$ in radius, $2$--$13\%$ in age, and below $0.6\%$ in helium-core mass and below $0.2\%$ in helium-core radius. Surface-effect corrections are negligible for g-dominated mixed modes, validating $\chi^2_{l=1g}$ as a robust fitting metric. For KIC~9475697, the core rotation rate is determined to be $\Omega_{\rm core} = 0.6945 \pm 0.0190\,\mu$Hz from model-based trapping parameters.

new.title: Estimation Of The Mass And The Spin Of The Neutron Star 4U 1728-34 Using Triples Of X-Ray Quasi-Periodic Oscillations
new.summary: X-ray quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) were reported for 19 different observations of the atoll source 4U 1728- 34. Three of them reveal triplets of QPOs: a lower and a upper kHz QPOs and a low-frequency QPO. Even though they are discernible only after averaging we assume them to be simultaneous. We apply a separate model (formula) for each of the three frequencies of the observed QPOs and compose a system which contains three algebraic equations for the three unknown parameters - the mass and the specific angular momentum of the central neutron star, and the radius of the orbit of orgin of the given triplet of QPOs, which allows us to find the numerical values of the later. Error propagation formulas are applied for the obtaining of interval estimates of the parameters of the star. This is done through implicit function differentiation. The calculations are repeated with several different models for the kHz QPOs.

new.title: Introducing the GION Lightcone Simulation Suite for Multi-Wavelength Large-Scale Structure Cosmology
new.summary: We present the GION (Ginkaku Lightcone Multi-wavelength Simulation Project) simulation suite: 10 full-sky high-resolution cosmological lightcone simulations and their associated products for multi-wavelength large-scale structure cosmology. We use the TreePM $N$-body code GINKAKU, which is highly optimized in the massively parallel environment, and integrate the on-the-fly lightcone construction technique. Each lightcone simulation is run with $6144^3$ particles in a volume of $(1.5 \, h^{-1} \, \mathrm{Gpc})^3$, which corresponds to a particle mass of $1.28 \times 10^9 \, h^{-1} \, \mathrm{M}_\odot$, and extends to $z = 5$. The fine mass resolution and the depth of the lightcone simulations allow us to resolve dark matter halos down to $10^{11} \, h^{-1} \, \mathrm{M}_\odot$ in the high-redshift Universe, which is crucial for applications to the Stage-IV cosmological surveys. The fundamental statistics of the simulations, including the matter power spectrum, halo power spectrum, and halo mass function, are validated against theoretical predictions. We also generate various large-scale structure observables from the lightcone outputs: the dark matter halo catalogs, mock galaxy samples, weak lensing convergence maps, and thermal and kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ and kSZ) maps. The angular power spectra of these observables, including the cross-correlation between weak lensing and the tSZ effect, are in good agreement with theoretical predictions, demonstrating that the suite provides mutually consistent multi-wavelength observables on the same lightcone. The GION simulation suite will be publicly available and can be used for various cosmological analyses to address the observational systematic effects and validate theoretical models.

new.title: A comprehensive reanalysis of HD 99458. Not a magnetic Ap star but an oscillating Algol with ongoing mass transfer
new.summary: Context. Since 2019, HD 99458 has been known as a unique example of a $\delta$ Sct variable with chemical peculiarities of Ap type in an eclipsing binary. Aims. We aim to review the peculiar status of the star with new observational materials. Methods. The current study is the result of meticulous analysis of space-based photometry from Kepler K2 and TESS, multi-site spectroscopic and spectropolarimetric observations, as well as speckle-interferometric data. Asteroseismic modelling of stellar pulsation is an essential part of the research. Results. We find HD 99458 to be an eclipsing Algol-type system with active mass transfer from the cool companion filling its Roche lobe to the pulsating primary. We identified signatures of a disc and accretion with varying rates in spectra and light curves. The system's orbital period increases with the rate $\dot{P}_\mathrm{orb}$ of 5.045 s yr$^{-1}$, indicating potential multiplicity. We failed to detect traces of the primary's magnetic field or excessive abundances, both of which are necessary to classify HD 99458 as an Ap star. We have constrained the fundamental parameters of the pulsating primary and analysed its pulsation using asteroseismology. In space-based photometry, we identified pulsation modes with angular degree $\ell\leq3$. Two-dimensional Fourier analysis of spectroscopic time series reveals pulsations in the form of standing waves with the azimuthal orders $|m|=5\pm1$. Combined analysis of photometry and spectroscopy confirms the status of HD 99458 as a triaxial gravitationally distorted pulsator. Conclusions. Our comprehensive study affirms the new classification for HD 99458.

new.title: Binary Dynamics and Mergers in a Stellar Disk and the Formation of Dusty Objects in the Galactic Center
new.summary: For more than a decade, observers have been tracking a population of enigmatic dusty objects orbiting the central supermassive black hole of the Milky Way, Sagittarius A$^\star$ (SgrA$^\star$). In one interpretation, these objects are products of stellar mergers enshrouded in gaseous-dusty envelopes, which account for their infrared excess, emission lines, and stability against the tidal forces of SgrA$^\star$. Recent near-infrared observations of D9, one of the dusty objects, revealed that it embeds a spectroscopic stellar binary. In this work, we present full-fledged N-body simulations of an eccentric disk of binary stars similar to the young stellar disk observed around SgrA$^\star$. We find that some of the binaries in the disk are naturally drawn towards SgrA$^\star$ and merge there due to Kozai-Lidov (KL) oscillations in their orbits. Together with the observed nature of D9, these findings represent a self-consistent picture of how the population of the observed dusty objects could have been brought into existence. The binary fraction in our N-body model evolves to increase with distance from SgrA$^\star$, which is also in agreement with the observational constraints. Our simulations also suggest that beside the dusty objects, stellar mergers are present within the young stellar disk, which could be identified as chemically peculiar or fast-rotating stars. Our results show that dynamical evolution of binary stars in the young stellar disk plays a crucial role in shaping the stellar content in the Galactic Center.

new.title: Local Analogs of Little Red Dots: Clues to the X-ray Weakness
new.summary: A major question about JWST's little red dots (LRDs) at $z\sim4-8$ is the origin of their apparent X-ray weakness. Even deep Chandra stacks yield only tentative detections or broad-band limits and cannot distinguish among super-Eddington accretion, intrinsic X-ray weakness, and Compton-thick (CT) obscuration. Local analogs offer a powerful complementary route. At $z\sim0.3$, similarly luminous sources require $\sim10^{3-4}$ less exposure for comparable signal-to-noise, suffer less source confusion, and directly probe the diagnostic rest-frame soft X-rays. Here we present a pilot Einstein Probe/FXT study of six "local little red dots" (LLRDs), V-shaped broad-line green pea galaxies selected as low-redshift counterparts of LRDs. These sources show X-ray diversity: "X-normal" LLRDs resemble type 1 AGNs in X-ray luminosity and optical variability, whereas the "X-weak" stack lies $\sim0.5-0.7$ dex below standard unobscured-quasar scaling relations while remaining compatible with the representative LRD stack and 95% of published individual limits. The X-weak LLRDs also lack detected optical variability and have redder optical continua than X-normal LLRDs, making their V-shaped SEDs closer to those of high-redshift LRDs. The detection of the X-weak stack at $\sim3.3\sigma$ with the soft-X-ray-sensitive EP-FXT provides rest-frame $\sim2-3$ keV constraints difficult to reconcile with a typical unobscured super-Eddington model or a local-AGN-like CT geometry examined here, although modified variants remain possible. The simplest alternative is a mildly X-ray-weak corona ($\Delta\alpha_{\mathrm{ox}}\sim-0.1$ to $-0.2$) with Compton-thin absorption ($N_{\mathrm{H}}\sim10^{22-23}$ cm$^{-2}$), consistent with the independent Balmer decrement/break diagnostics. Together with growing samples of local LRD analogs, our results offer a practical path for testing the physical nature of LRD X-ray weakness.

new.title: Luminosity-weighted galaxy and gravitational wave cross-correlations
new.summary: Cross-correlations of galaxies and gravitational waves (GW) can be used to extract cosmological parameters and the gravitational wave bias. In this work, we study how to include galaxy luminosities in these spatial cross-correlations, inspired by the standard approach of dark sirens line-of-sight redshift priors. We present a formalism to include luminosity information in galaxy-GW simulations and study the effects of assigning a hosting probability that depends on luminosity through a simple power law $p_{\rm{host}} \propto L^\beta$ with $\beta \in \{0,1,2\}$ corresponding to uniformly, linear and quadratically weighted in luminosity. This effectively changes the GW linear bias with respect to dark matter and, in principle, allows to gain signal-to-noise and a sharper measurement of cosmological parameters. For a realistic luminosity dependence of the galaxy bias taken from DESI data, the gain is marginal, making the method robust to different luminosity weighting prescriptions. We show that the cross-correlation inference is able to recover the injected GW bias within $10\%$ if there is a mismatch between the injected linear bias of host galaxies and observed galaxies, provided that one sticks to relatively large scales. We also show that the Hubble constant and matter energy density can be recovered to $0.5\%$ and $5\%$ respectively with a third generation network of GW detectors, regardless of the modeling of the GW bias.

new.title: Star clusters at cosmic dawn I: the emergence of the initial cluster mass function
new.summary: JWST observations of lensed galaxies reveal unusually bright star-cluster candidates within the first billion years after the Big Bang. However, the physical processes shaping the initial cluster mass function (ICMF) remain uncertain. We study the formation of a galaxy embedded in a dark matter halo whose virial mass reaches $10^{10} \mathrm{M}_\odot$ at $z=6$, using cosmological radiation-hydrodynamics zoom-in simulations. Its star clusters, represented by sink particles, accrete gas and form stellar populations that supply radiation and supernova feedback, thereby regulating their own growth. As we do not prescribe an efficiency per free-fall time or a fixed star-cluster formation duration, the ICMF emerges self-consistently. We assess the effects of numerical resolution and stellar radiation. Schechter fits to the central-galaxy ICMF give truncation masses near $6 \times 10^6 \mathrm{M}_\odot$, with substantial uncertainty. At fixed resolution, including stellar radiation makes the low-mass slope of the ICMF shallower, from $-1.60$ to $-1.34$, while doubling the spatial resolution steepens it back to $-1.54$. Stellar radiation also reduces the abundance of low-mass clouds, particularly those with lower gas densities, and shortens the formation time of star clusters to about a Myr, i.e. well before their first supernovae go off. On average, more rapidly fed star clusters accrete for longer, making their final masses rise faster than linearly with the initial accretion rate and contributing to a flatter ICMF. At fixed host-galaxy star formation rate, our brightest simulated clusters reach UV luminosities comparable to those of observed lensed star-cluster candidates.

new.title: Comparison of observed and theoretically calculated amplitudes of Forbush effects for events associated with the arrival of a shock wave
new.summary: This paper examines the role of plasma compression regions ahead of interplanetary coronal mass ejections in the formation of Forbush effects decreases in cosmic ray intensity during the first phase. The aim of this study is to identify and quantify the relationship between the structure of the CME (specifically, the parameters of the compression region behind the shock front) and the nature of the observed Forbush effect. To this end, events with intensity decrease amplitudes greater than 5 percent were selected, and a theoretical model of cosmic ray behavior at the shock front was tested using modern analytical methods and mathematical models. Analysis of the results for two dozen events revealed satisfactory agreement between the theory and observations. The key reason for some discrepancies is the need to integrate the magnetic field over the particle gyro radius. The obtained data provide insight into the mechanisms of cosmic ray modulation in such environments.

new.title: The MIRI/MRS Library. III. Detector-based optimal spectral extraction and high-contrast imaging applications
new.summary: (Abridged) JWST has now been operational for five years, and the associated data reduction pipelines have reached maturity. For MIRI/MRS, one can generally get a good-quality spectrum by simply running the standard pipeline, especially for unresolved sources. However, users are starting to look deeper into the data, trying to detect the smallest features in the faintest objects, and find close companions. Following the corrections derived in Papers I and II in this series, we now introduce a novel way to extract MIRI/MRS spectra: from the detectors directly. Currently the most common way to analyse data from integral field spectrometers is to reconstruct a spectral cube from the detector images. Theoretically, detector-extracted spectra could reach higher S/N, and better handle bad pixels. We generate stable and well-sampled PSF models using the sub-pixel scan of calibration star 10 Lac observed in PID 3779. These PSFs were used in a detector-based optimal extraction algorithm building on past approaches, where the contributions per pixel were weighted by their noise properties and contribution to the total illumination. The PSF models were used to subtract the PSF of a bright central source from the detector, both by direct subtraction, and a PCA approach. We find that our optimal setup allows us to get a $>$1.5 times higher S/N compared to the standard pipeline cube extraction. However, we approximately matched more involved cube processing. We were able to subtract the PSF to sub-percent levels, allowing us to extract spectra from faint companions. The novel approach greatly improves on the current standard pipeline reduction. We have not yet reached the fundamental noise limits. There are clear points of improvement that can be addressed using additional data. We demonstrate that detector-based processing of MIRI/MRS data has great potential.

new.title: The Galactic rotation curve from the ALS III catalogue of OB Stars
new.summary: The Galactic rotation curve reveals the radial mass distribution of the Milky Way, but its determination depends on the tracer population. Young massive stars are the least dynamically evolved tracer, retaining the kinematics of the gas from which they formed, yet previous determinations from OB stars were confined to the solar neighbourhood. We determine the rotation curve and the solar motion from 14017 spectroscopically confirmed OB stars from the ALS III catalogue, using Gaia DR3 five-dimensional astrometry with revised distances and corrected proper motions. The curve is parameterised as a fourth-degree Chebyshev polynomial in Galactocentric radius and fitted to the proper motions by weighted least squares, solving simultaneously for the solar motion. Uncertainties are derived from 1000 bootstrap resamplings. We obtain a circular velocity at the solar radius (8.178 kpc) of 236.3 +/- 1.1 km/s, solar motion components U = 8.06 +/- 0.41, V = 10.91 +/- 0.86 and W = 7.53 +/- 0.14 km/s, and Oort constants A = 16.35 +/- 0.21 and B = -12.54 +/- 0.19 km/s/kpc. The curve rises inside the solar circle and declines gently beyond it, with a local gradient of -3.81 +/- 0.38 km/s/kpc, and is constrained between 5.5 and 11 kpc. Because the tracer is dynamically cold and the proper motions are fitted directly, no asymmetric drift correction or Jeans modelling is required, so the systematics differ from those affecting older tracers. The gentle decline beyond the solar radius agrees with determinations from older tracers where they overlap, making it unlikely to be a methodological artefact. Only the solar radial motion is poorly constrained by tangential data, without affecting the curve. The stars departing most from the curve (1474 to 1662, depending on the selection criterion) form the largest sample of OB runaway candidates to date, to be analysed in a forthcoming paper based on Gaia DR4.

new.title: Accuracy of electric current inference assuming three-dimensional hydrostatic equilibrium
new.summary: The chromospheric and coronal heating problem is among the major open questions in solar physics. Some of the possible mechanisms that can explain the rise in temperature that is needed to reproduce the observations require the estimation of electric currents. Since these depend on the spatial derivatives of the magnetic field components, it is necessary to obtain the full magnetic field vector from observational data in a 3D geometrical grid. We developed a new method to obtain the 3D geometrical configuration of the atmosphere using the approximation of hydrostatic equilibrium in three dimensions to determine the gas pressure and density as a function of optical depth, column mass, or geometrical distance. This development has been designed as an extension for any inversion code that outputs a stratification of temperature and gas pressure or density to enable the estimation of electric current densities from observations. We investigated our approach using a snapshot from a sunspot MHD simulation. The difference between the solver output and the simulation, taken as the ground truth, is mostly between 30 and 45 %, showing a similar pattern over a large optical depth range. Additional tests also showed that the solver provides a unique solution, has a scarce sensitivity to the boundary condition and is only marginally impacted by the viewing angle. We conclude that the electric currents can be inferred at a reasonable accuracy with this approach using the simulation parameters as input. We also tested set-ups that aim at mimicking more realistic cases, where the code performed equally well. The results in this work show promise with respect to future applications to spectropolarimetric data, however, some additional challenges will need to be adressed when moving from the controlled input of the simulation to observational data.

new.title: Forward model of the Gaia DR3 selection function
new.summary: The completeness of an astronomical catalogue depends on its selection function, which is a combination of the observing strategy, instrumental characteristics, and intrinsic properties of the sources being observed. This is particularly complex for Gaia, whose non-uniform scanning law and onboard prioritisation of bright sources in dense areas make its selection function vary strongly with celestial position and source brightness. We estimate the Gaia DR3 source catalogue selection function across the whole sky and over the full magnitude range, using only data from the Gaia catalogue and knowledge of the nominal scanning law as provided by the Gaia Observation Forecast Tool. We develop a hierarchical Bayesian model that estimates the number of times Gaia scanned each celestial position jointly with the source detection efficiency, and fit it via Markov chain Monte Carlo to the 1 806 196 447 sources in Gaia DR3 with reported celestial positions, G magnitudes, and astrometric matched transit counts. Gaia DR3 is essentially complete for G in (5, 19.5) in the on-sky median. After that, the completeness decreases with magnitude according to the scanning law pattern combined with the imprint of crowded regions. The completeness is also lower at the very bright end of the survey, consistent with the known limitations on Gaia observations of bright stars. We find an unexpected completeness increase beyond G ~ 21, which we conclude is an artefact caused by extended sources, as confirmed by cross-matching against Euclid's Q1 catalogue. Treating the scanning law as part of the inference process, and anchoring it to all Gaia DR3 sources of all magnitudes on a fine-grained grid on the sky, removes the need for an explicit crowding correction. The resulting selection function, valid everywhere where Gaia data are available, is released as part of the GaiaUnlimited Python package. [abridged]

new.title: Polarization Observations of NGC 315 with FAST
new.summary: We present new continuum and polarization observations of radio galaxy NGC 315 obtained with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) over 1.0-1.5 GHz. The FAST data detect diffuse large-scale polarized emission with a noise level of 0.065 mJy beam$^{-1}$ at resolution of $4'$. We derived a rotation measure (RM) map with an error of 1.1 rad m$^{-2}$ including systematic error. The intrinsic RM map was obtained after subtracting the Galactic foreground contribution. We estimated a total magnetic field strength of $\lesssim 1$ $\mu$G across the source and a thermal electron density of $\sim 10^{-4}$ cm$^{-3}$ toward the northwest lobe. The fractional polarization analysis suggests a random magnetic-field component over a large area toward the northwest lobe.

new.title: Spatial distribution of star formation in dwarf galaxies: Merger-driven and secular starburst
new.summary: Galaxy interactions can induce bursts of star formation (SF), while internal or secular processes can also trigger starbursts (SB). Recent studies of the spatial distribution of SF in high-mass (M$_{*}>10^{10}M_{\odot}$) SB galaxies show that SF is centrally concentrated in merger-driven SBs, whereas in secularly driven SB systems, SF is uniformly enhanced across the system. However, it is not clear whether such distinct spatial signatures are present in low-mass (M$_{*} < 10^{10} M_{\odot}$) SB galaxies. In this context, we studied the SF properties of a sample of 272 isolated SB (i.e., with no massive galaxy, within a 1 Mpc$^3$ volume) dwarf galaxies consisting of 17 post-merger and 255 non-interacting SB galaxies, spanning a stellar mass range of $10^{7}-10^{9.6} M_{\odot}$ and a redshift range of 0.01-0.12. For this study, we utilise FUV imaging data from GALEX to estimate the star formation rates of our sample galaxies. We investigated the spatial variation of SB activity by comparing star formation rate surface density (SFRD) across radial bins for post-merger and non-interacting samples of dwarfs. We find an enhancement in SFRD across all radial bins for both samples, and that the enhancement is more or less uniform across the galaxy, within uncertainties. This indicates that SF in low-mass SB galaxies is uniformly enhanced throughout the galaxy, regardless of the mechanism that triggers the SB. This contrasts with observations in massive galaxies, where SF is centrally concentrated in merger-driven SB systems. The lack of central concentration of SF in low-mass merger systems could be due to their shallow gravitational potentials and the compression of extended gaseous envelopes during interactions, which trigger SF across these galaxies. Deeper, higher-spatial-resolution observations are essential for better understanding the spatial distribution of SF in low-mass galaxies.

new.title: Magnetic Reconnection Modifies Cosmic-Ray Transport in the Interstellar Medium
new.summary: We present numerical magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of the interstellar medium in gravity-stratified boxes with the Piernik MHD code. The system contains thermal gas, spectrally resolved cosmic-ray (CR) nuclei within the CRESP algorithm, and spectrally unresolved CR protons. CR protons drive gas outflows and undergo Coulomb and hadronic losses. CR nuclei undergo Coulomb losses. We also include the spallation of primary Carbon by thermal gas atoms, thereby decaying Car- bon into secondary stable Boron isotopes. We use the resistive-MHD approximation as a subgrid model for unresolved turbulent magnetic dissipation in current sheets. We perform a parameter study of the magnetic diffusivity {\eta}. The Boron-to-Carbon ratio B/C and hadronic {\gamma}-ray luminosity density are computed as diagnostics. We find that non-zero magnetic diffusivity modifies the magnetic topology, leading to a more horizontal field in the halo, thereby accumulating CRs in the disk region and signifi- cantly increasing the CR escape time. As a consequence, the local turbulent conditions and turbulent reconnection in the interstellar medium should be considered when interpreting B/C and hadronic {\gamma}-ray luminosity observed at Earth. Our results suggest that the escape time and diffusion coefficient of CRs deduced from observational data in the vicinity of the Solar System cannot be extrapolated to the whole Galaxy.
