new.title: Tracking the Evolution of Supermassive Black Hole Binaries with Pulsar Terms
new.summary: Pulsar timing arrays will soon be able to resolve the loudest supermassive black hole binaries contributing to the stochastic gravitational wave background at nanohertz frequencies. While the few decades of observations are typically not enough to see these binaries evolve in frequency, the so-called pulsar terms offer a glimpse into the past and can help us map out the frequency evolution of these binaries over tens of thousands of years. Measuring this long-term frequency evolution can allow us to look for deviations from a vacuum binary evolution due to various environmental effects. We develop a Fisher-matrix approach to calculate how precisely the frequency can be tracked over time in this manner, and demonstrate its use on a realistic near-future pulsar timing array with a 30-year baseline. We find that the environmental effects predicted by 2-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations of circumbinary disks are unlikely to be detectable in the circular binaries we considered, however, in some cases they might result in biased chirp mass recovery if ignored. We also demonstrate how this approach allows one to test the orbital evolution predicted by general relativity in a purely gravitational-wave driven inspiral, and to put upper limits on additional generic environmental effects described by a power-law hardening model.

new.title: Systematic Slopes in NIRSpec BOTS Observations
new.summary: We investigate empirical white light and spectroscopic trends in the temporal systematic slopes seen in NIRSpec Bright Object Time Series (BOTS) observations. Using a sample of 14 high-resolution G395H (dispersed across both the NRS1 and NRS2 detectors) and 10 low-resolution Prism (dispersed across NRS1 only) transit light curves, we measured the visit-long, pre-transit, and post-transit slopes. For the G395H white light curves, we find a correlation between the G395H NRS1 systematic slope and the host star magnitude, as well as the number of groups per integration. We also note that the systematic slopes vary with time over the course of a given time-series, with steeper pre-transit slopes compared to post-transit. These trends in the white light slopes are not apparent for G395H NRS2 or Prism. At the spectroscopic light curve level, the NRS1 and Prism slopes show a distinct wavelength-dependent signature across the full sample with the largest slopes between ~3-3.4 microns. At these wavelengths, the brightest targets display the strongest chromatic slope signatures. The NRS2 slopes show no apparent chromaticity across the full sample.

new.title: ARENA: Active Region attENtion Aggregation for interpretable solar flare prediction
new.summary: Predicting solar flares is a challenging space-weather forecasting problem with potentially significant impacts on Earth's upper atmosphere, including disruptions to radio communications. We propose Active Region attENtion Aggregation (ARENA), a neural network architecture that predicts solar flares from a variable number of active-region cutouts while learning to identify the region most relevant to the prediction. ARENA is trained using multiple-instance learning under weak supervision, requiring only a flare/no-flare label for the observation and no labels specifying the flare origin. The learned attention mechanism therefore provides a means of localizing the active region driving the prediction without explicit origin annotations. ARENA achieves a heidke skill score of 0.45 which is comparable to other flare prediction approaches. These results demonstrate that active-region-based aggregation can provide an efficient and interpretable approach to solar flare prediction. The code is available at this https URL .

new.title: Probing the star-forming environment of GRB across cosmic ages with high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy: From \textit{XMM-Newton}/RGS and \textit{XRISM}/Resolve to \textit{NewAthena}/X-IFU
new.summary: Optical and infrared GRB absorption spectroscopy provides valuable insight into host-galaxy properties across cosmic time. However, the star-forming region embedding the progenitor, on scales $\lesssim 100~\mathrm{pc}$ is heavily ionized by the GRB emission, making X-ray spectroscopy the sole probe of its physical and chemical conditions. We characterize the GRB-embedding medium as a function of progenitor type and cosmic epoch via high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy. We extend our study to high-redshift GRBs to evaluate how effectively X-ray absorption signatures can distinguish between pristine, Pop~III-, and Pop~II-enriched environments. Using the time-dependent photoionization code \texttt{TEPID}, we self-consistently calculate the ionization structure of the absorber, the energies and the strengths of the resulting absorption lines. We analyze a flux-selected sample of GRBs showing strong evidence for time-dependent photoionization, and search for predicted narrow features in the RGS spectra. We also assess the performance of \textit{XRISM}/Resolve and \textit{NewAthena}/X-IFU in detecting these features. In the single archival case with sufficient RGS signal-to-noise ratio (GRB~090618 at $z=0.54$), we find $\approx 3\sigma$ combined evidence for narrow, highly ionized Fe~L absorption lines. For bright nearby GRBs, \textit{XRISM}/Resolve can detect Fe~K absorption lines even in its current gate-valve-closed configuration ($\sim 3$ expected events/yr). \textit{NewAthena}/X-IFU will enable systematic population studies of GRB environments, delivering redshifts with precision comparable to optical/IR spectroscopy, unaffected by dust obscuration and Ly-$\alpha$ forest absorption. Crucially, it will precisely diagnose the density, size, metallicity, and abundance patterns, ultimately revealing whether high-$z$ GRBs originate in pristine, Pop~III-, or Pop~II-enriched media.

new.title: Joint Angular-Power Distributions of Interfering Nanohertz Gravitational Waves
new.summary: Finite populations of supermassive black-hole binaries produce fluctuations in both gravitational-wave power and pulsar timing correlations. We characterize the realization-dependent, orientation-averaged Earth-term angular correlation through its frequency-resolved Legendre coefficients. A hybrid model of bright sources and a Gaussian faint background extends the conditional Gamma distribution in the many-weak-source limit to non-central $\chi^2$ statistics, yielding correlated multipoles after population marginalization. Our analytical variance decomposition and SMBHB population simulations reveal a population-dependent transition from interference dominated variance at low frequencies to population-power-dominated variance at high frequencies. In the many-weak-source regime, a multivariate lognormal approximation captures the main features of the joint distribution using only the first two log-cumulants. These results provide statistical benchmarks for fluctuations in both the overall amplitude and angular structure of the realized correlation.

new.title: The GAPS Programme at TNG LXXXI. The puzzle of the HeI absorption signal in the atmosphere of V1298 Tau b with GIARPS@TNG
new.summary: Atmospheric escape shapes close-in planets mostly in their first tens of Myr. The young V1298Tau system (10-30Myr) is a benchmark for investigating photoevaporation and planetary evolution at early stages. The metastable HeI near-infrared triplet is a key proxy for atmospheric escape. We aim to detect and characterise HeI in the extended atmosphere of V1298Taub. We analysed four transits over a 4-year baseline using GIARPS (GIANO-B + HARPS-N) at the Telescopio Nazionale Galileo. We re-derived the projected spin-orbit angle by modelling the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect. Using simultaneous optical and near-infrared high-resolution transmission spectroscopy of V1298Taub, we monitored the HeI triplet alongside key chromospheric indicators ($\log R'_{HK}$, H$\alpha$, and NaI) to disentangle stellar activity from planetary evaporation. While the stellar spectra show significant night-to-night variability, transmission spectroscopy reveals persistent HeI absorption across all four epochs. This contrasts with H$\alpha$ and NaI, observed over two nights with simultaneous HARPS-N monitoring, which fluctuate between emission and absorption due to stellar activity. The consistent presence of HeI over 4 years may suggest a planetary origin, despite stellar-driven depth modulation. ATES hydrodynamic simulations show that stellar XUV flux variations modulate the HeI absorption depth and equivalent width. Furthermore, stellar wind fluctuations likely drive the observed night-to-night variability of the exospheric structure. The detection of HeI across all epochs may support planetary evaporation, despite modulation by stellar activity. Our results underscore that disentangling a planetary signal from stellar contamination remains challenging for highly active hosts; securing the planetary nature of the HeI signature requires activity monitoring and full transit coverage to establish a robust baseline.

new.title: Research of signs of star formation in three S0 galaxies - members of isolated pairs
new.summary: We obtained and analyzed long-slit spectra of three lenticular galaxies with optical rings: PGC 48114, ESO 234-011, and ESO 444-076. Ionized gas was detected in all of them. In PGC 48114, the excitation mechanism of the ionized gas differs along the ring, despite the consistent kinematics of the ionized gas and stars, as we showed earlier. Narrow-band images of PGC 48114 in the H$\alpha$ and [NII]$\lambda$6583 emission lines revealed a star formation arc in the northwestern part of the ring. In ESO 234-011 and ESO 444-076, the ionized gas along the long slit is shock-excited and have kinematic discrepancy with the stars. This implies accretion of matter at an angle to the main disk of the S0 galaxies, which likely inhibits ongoing star formation. The companions of these S0 galaxies are late-type galaxies with extensive ongoing star formation. These companions may be the sources of the gas, or each pair may be feeding from a common gas reservoir.

new.title: Diversity of planetary origins and compositions traced by stellar abundance differences of co-natal star systems
new.summary: Co-natal stars, wide binaries that form from the same molecular cloud, should harbor the same stellar composition. Observations indicate stellar abundance differences in a small fraction of these co-natal systems. The stellar abundance differences have been attributed to the ingestion of planets by their host stars. We analyze a previous sample of co-natal stars to determine the composition of the planets that were ingested. The abundance differences in these co-natal pairs can show a positive abundance difference of the refractory elements (Fe, Mg, Si) paired with a positive, zero, or negative abundance difference of volatiles (O, C, S). Positive trends of refractory and volatile abundance differences can be explained (at minimum) with the ingestion of a single planet by one of the stars. Positive trends of refractory abundance differences paired with zero or negative abundance differences of oxygen and carbon imply that both stars are required to ingest planets formed at different locations (interior/exterior to the water and/or C-grain evaporation front). Some systems show a sulfur abundance difference that is a factor of a few lower than the abundance difference of Fe, Si, and Mg, even though sulfur is accreted via the moderately volatile compound FeS. This can be explained by the migration of one of the planets across the FeS evaporation front, where the planet first accretes large amounts of sulfur and then no sulfur, while still accreting the other refractory elements before being ingested by its host star. Our study shows that the planetary compositions derived from the detailed stellar abundances can explain the measured abundance differences of co-natal stars, giving a handle on the composition of exoplanets. At the same time it implies very different planetary compositions caused by the different formation location of these planets, in agreement with planet formation models.

new.title: The Physics of the Cold and Warm Interstellar Medium Through Radio Recombination Lines
new.summary: The interplay between star formation and the interstellar medium (ISM) gives rise to a feedback cycle that is one of the key drivers of galaxy evolution. The coldest gas in the ISM provides the fuel for star formation, and, in turn, the ISM is affected by feedback in the form of photons, shocks, and cosmic rays. Radio recombination lines (RRLs) offer a unique way of characterizing the gas in the ISM as extinction free probes of the gas kinematics, density, temperature, and radiation field. Hydrogen RRLs (HRRLs) probe gas where hydrogen is ionized, while carbon RRLs (CRRLs) probe cold gas in the HI-to-H$_{2}$ transition layers. The superb sensitivity, spatial resolution, large field of view, and frequency resolution and coverage of the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) will allow for efficient observations of RRLs, that will make significant impacts to the study of the diffuse ISM. By observing RRLs with the SKA we will be able to determine the thermal and turbulent balance, chemical enrichment, sizes, and ionization rate of the cold and ionized gases from degree-scales down to arcsecond scales in our Galaxy.

new.title: Modelling kNN-CDFs of biased tracers in redshift space using hybrid Lagrangian bias expansion
new.summary: Higher-order statistics are becoming increasingly useful in clustering studies of the large-scale structure (LSS) of the universe. The kNN-CDFs are one such higher-order statistic, sensitive to all N-point correlations and easy to compute on data. Utilising their statistical gains for cosmological inference requires modelling them accurately for the tracer of interest. We use the hybrid Lagrangian bias expansion to enable this modelling in redshift space, building and validating the pipeline on Quijote simulations. We show that the kNN-CDFs of a luminous red galaxy (LRG)-like sample can be modelled down to scales as small as r = 10 Mpc/h, with the minimum reliable scale increasing with nearest-neighbour order. Moreover, the model parameters inferred from the kNN-CDFs also describe the galaxy power spectrum P(k), indicating model consistency across the two statistics and the feasibility of combining them. Fisher forecasts for galaxy auto clustering show that combining P(k) and kNN-CDFs improves constraints on all parameters relative to either statistic alone. Relative to P(k), the constraints on $b_3$ improve the most, while those on $\sigma_8$ and $\Omega_m$ improve by factors of 3.5 and 1.7, respectively. Including galaxy-matter cross clustering alongside galaxy auto clustering further improves the Fisher constraints from both P(k) and kNN-CDFs, with their combination yielding the tightest constraints overall. Relative to P(k), the largest improvement from this combination is found for $b_2$, while the constraints on $\sigma_8$ and $\Omega_m$ improve by factors of 4.2 and 1.7, respectively. These results demonstrate the applicability of the hybrid Lagrangian bias framework to model the kNN-CDFs of biased tracers in redshift space, and the potential of combining higher-order and two-point statistics to extract cosmological information.

new.title: Physics Informed Neural Network for Multi-dimensional Turbulent Self-gravitating Flows
new.summary: Molecular clouds exhibit complex, multi-scale dynamics driven by the interplay of turbulence, self-gravity, and gas pressure. Modelling these systems with conventional grid-based methods becomes increasingly expensive as spatial resolution and dimensionality increase. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free alternative by incorporating the governing equations directly into the training objective, but their ability to model realistic turbulent self-gravitating flows remains largely unexplored. We apply PINNs to isothermal molecular clouds initialized with astrophysically motivated turbulent velocity fields, considering subsonic and supersonic evolution in two and three dimensions. We benchmark the predicted density and velocity fields against the finite-volume code Athena++. PINNs accurately recover the global evolution of the flow over multiple free-fall times across turbulent realizations, Mach numbers, and dimensionalities. Their training cost also exhibits weak dependence on spatial resolution, increasing by less than 25% from 128^3 to 1024^3 in our experiments. These results demonstrate that PINNs can model substantially more realistic self-gravitating turbulent flows than previously explored and provide a promising complementary framework for studying these systems.

new.title: The Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess and the Look-Elsewhere Effect
new.summary: The origin of the excess of GeV gamma-rays in the Milky Way's galactic center observed by Fermi-LAT has been an open question for nearly two decades. The two leading interpretations of this signal are that it is produced either by annihilating dark matter (DM), or arises from unresolved point sources, such as a novel population of millisecond pulsars. In both scenarios, uncertainties and limitations in the modeling of galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission, such as the steady-state approximation of cosmic ray (CR) propagation and assumption of an axisymmetric distribution of CRs, complicate the interpretation of the galactic center excess (GCE). Simulations with full magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) and CR transport can provide a new avenue for understanding the astrophysical phenomena that drive galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission. We utilize MHD simulations of Milky Way analogs with time-dependent, spectrally-resolved CR transport to reconstruct diffuse gamma-ray emission. Comparing instantaneous emission to a time-averaged baseline, we find residuals up to several times larger than the Fermi GCE, with a wide range of spectral shapes and spatial morphologies. At some simulation snapshots, the spectrum and morphology of the residuals resemble the Fermi GCE. Our results suggest that the Fermi GCE may be a manifestation of the look-elsewhere effect- a transient fluctuation in diffuse emission from stellar sources, observed at an inopportune moment- and motivate the development of new Fermi-LAT analysis templates that account for time-dependent CR transport.

The shaded regions indicate the full range of spectra over the same time span. The measured Fermi-LAT γ \gamma -ray spectrum in the same ROI of the Milky Way is shown by the black dotted line. While features of the γ \gamma -ray spectra for the simulated galaxies show similarities to the measured spectrum, such as a peak below 1 GeV and a similar slope of the high-energy tail, the simulated spectra are an order-of-magnitude larger, due to the greater number of stellar sources of CRs in the simulations compared to the Milky Way. new.title: GRB 260924A: Extreme Energetics, Bright GeV Emission, and Exceptional X-ray and Optical Luminosity
new.summary: We present a multiwavelength study of GRB~260924A at $z=3.51\pm0.10$ using \textit{Fermi}, \textit{Swift}, and ground-based optical and near-infrared observations. Its isotropic-equivalent gamma-ray energy, $E_{\gamma,\mathrm{iso}}\simeq9.79\times10^{54}$~erg, places it among the most energetic GRBs observed. The prompt emission comprised two bright episodes separated by weaker activity. The X-ray afterglow ranked among the most luminous in our comparison sample at selected post-flare epochs, with a luminosity comparable to that of GRB~221009A at a rest-frame time of 3.5~ks. At a common redshift of $z=1$, the optical afterglow outshone GRB~221009A by approximately 2~mag at 0.3~d and 1~mag near 1~d. LAT emission extended to approximately 1100~s and showed an early excess above the subsequent decay. The highest-energy photon, 43.3~GeV, arrived at 82~s during the first episode; a 14.2~GeV photon arrived at 304~s between episodes. We describe the afterglow light curves through forward-shock synchrotron and synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) emission, with reverse-shock SSC accounting for the early LAT excess. We connect the early and late afterglow phases by modelling the X-ray rebrightening at several kiloseconds through energy injection from trailing ejecta and evolving shock microphysics. The late afterglow suggests a stratified medium, modelled as $n(R)\propto R^{-1.2}$. Within this interpretation, the magnetic contrast $R_B\equiv(\varepsilon_{B,r}/\varepsilon_{B,f})^{1/2} \simeq2.6$ suggests magnetized ejecta, while the highest-energy LAT photons exceed the predicted synchrotron limit, supporting an SSC contribution.

new.title: The ALMA Survey of Gas Evolution of PROtoplanetary disks (AGE-PRO): Evolution of dust properties from multi-wavelength observations
new.summary: Understanding the evolution of solids in protoplanetary discs is important to comprehend the formation of giant planets cores and terrestrial planets. The ALMA Large Program AGE-PRO studied key disc properties in a survey of 30 protoplanetary discs across three evolutionary stages: the embedded phase (0.5-1 Myr), the middle-age phase (1-3 Myr), and the end of the disc lifetime (2-6 Myr). Preliminary dust properties were estimated using 1.3 mm observations, but a multi-wavelength analysis provides a better constraint of important properties such as the dust disc mass, the dust temperature, and the maximum grain size. We present new ALMA 3.1 mm and 1.5 mm (Bands 3 and 5) continuum observations of the complete survey of 30 AGE-PRO discs. We fitted the observed visibilities and derived radial brightness profiles, spatially resolving 20 discs from the AGE-PRO sample at the two studied wavelengths. A multi-wavelength modelling was performed including also the radial profiles from the 1.3 mm observations. Our results replicate trends obtained from the single wavelength analysis: the dust disc size seems to be constant over age and the dust disc mass decreases with time, with a factor $\sim$10-40 uncertainty from opacity assumptions. This result implies much lower gas-to-dust mass ratios for the discs in our sample than previously reported. In addition, the derived spectral indices are consistent with optically thick emission in a large fraction of the AGE-PRO discs, in particular for the Ophiuchus and Lupus discs.

new.title: Complete Multi-Band Structural Characterization for 10 Million Galaxies in the Hyper Suprime-Cam Wide Survey using Deep Learning
new.summary: Galaxy structure is wavelength-dependent, as different photometric bands trace distinct stellar populations and structural components. We present per-galaxy Bayesian posterior distributions of the bulge-to-total light ratio ($L_B/L_T$), effective radius ($R_e$), and flux ($F$) in the $g$, $r$, and $i$ bands for nearly $10$ million galaxies across $\sim$1400\,deg$^2$ of the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program (HSC-SSP) Wide survey at $z \leq 0.75$ and $m < 23$. To our knowledge, this is the largest multi-band catalog of bulge--disk structural parameters with per-galaxy posteriors. $\sim$3.9 million of the above galaxies have full multi-band coverage. Measurements are generated using the Galaxy Morphology Posterior Estimation Network (\gampen{}), a Bayesian deep-learning framework. We demonstrate that we can adapt \gampen{} from previously-trained single-band models to the new bands by using transfer learning on only $\sim$0.5\% of our dataset. Despite this extremely small training set, \gampen{} successfully reproduces light-profile fitting measurements and its output posteriors are extremely well-calibrated with $\lesssim6\%$ mean deviation. This approach offers a scalable pathway to structural parameter measurements with robust uncertainties for Rubin, Euclid, and Roman data, which we will pursue in forthcoming work. While structural measurements remain robust across most bands and redshift ranges, performance degrades significantly for the $g$-band at $z \gtrsim 0.5$, where it increasingly probes rest-frame ultraviolet emission; these measurements are therefore excluded from the public release. This public catalog will enable large-scale statistical studies of morphological color gradients, wavelength-dependent galaxy structure, and galaxy evolution.

new.title: A Population Synthesis Model for Odd Radio Circles Produced by Shock-Bubble Interactions
new.summary: Odd Radio Circles (ORCs) are edge-brightened rings of diffuse radio emission of roughly arcminute size whose physical origin remains debated. One proposed mechanism is vortex formation through Shock-Bubble interaction (SBI), in which a merger or accretion shock re-energizes a fossil radio lobe into an edge-brightened ring. We test whether this mechanism can reproduce the observed ORC abundance using a Monte Carlo population-synthesis model that combines the galaxy stellar mass function, the radio-AGN incidence relation, dark-matter halo merger histories, and the inflation and buoyant survival of AGN-inflated bubbles, with synthetic radio fluxes and ring geometries drawn from a grid of magnetohydrodynamic SBI simulations. Applying survey-specific selection to the ASKAP-EMU Pilot Survey (944 MHz) and the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey (LoTSS; 144 MHz), we predict $2.7^{+3.9}_{-1.6}$ detectable ORCs in the EMU Pilot, matching the three found there, and $268^{+331}_{-148}$ in LoTSS, of which $7.5^{+9.5}_{-4.2}$ have a counterpart at 1.4 GHz. The predicted hosts are mostly central galaxies in group-scale halos. The predicted rings are physically smaller and lie at lower redshifts than the galaxies identified as hosts of the known ORCs, suggesting that SBI produces mainly the nearby part of the ORC population, or that some ORCs are associated with the wrong host. The population synthesis model also predicts a large population of low surface brightness steep-spectrum ORCs in the LoTSS band, implying a large hidden population and predicting that deeper low-frequency surveys should uncover many more ORCs than are currently known. These results indicate that shock-bubble interactions can account for at least part of the observed incidence of ORCs.

new.title: One-Million-Year-Old Nascent Eclipsing Binaries in the LMC
new.summary: The light curves of nascent eclipsing binaries (EBs) feature sinusoidal reflection effects as a hot B-type main-sequence (MS) primary irradiates the near side of a cool, low-mass, pre-MS companion. We obtained multi-epoch echelle spectra with the MIKE spectrograph on the 6.5m Magellan-Clay Telescope of three nascent EBs embedded in H II regions within the LMC. By fitting atmospheric models to the spectra, the primaries are found to be mid-B dwarfs (T_eff,1 = 18,600-22,800 K; M_1 = 6.8-8.5 Msun). The dynamical masses of the secondaries are only M_2 = 0.38-0.95 Msun, yielding extremely small mass ratios q = M_2/M_1 = 0.05-0.11. Unlike solar-type primaries, which exhibit a dearth of close companions with q < 0.1 known as the brown dwarf desert, massive stars can readily form with very close companions below q < 0.1. By fitting PHOEBE models to the OGLE-III light curves, we measure the secondary radii R_2 = 2.0-2.8 Rsun and temperatures T_eff,2 = 4,000 K. The pre-MS companions are located high on the Hayashi track where evolutionary models indicate ages of only 1 Myr. Their extreme youth suggests that nascent EBs formed via inward disk migration during the previous embedded protostellar phase.

new.title: Three subpopulations of binary black holes in mass, spin magnitudes and tilts following GWTC-5
new.summary: The mass and spin distributions of merging binary black holes offer clues to their formation pathways, which remain uncertain. In this work, we model the population of binary black holes using generic subpopulations with distinct mass-ratio, spin-magnitude, and spin-tilt distributions, whose relative contributions vary with primary mass. Using the 259 binary black holes in the fifth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA catalog (GWTC-5), we resolve three subpopulations with low, medium, and high spins. The low-spin population dominates for primary masses near $35 M_\odot$, contributes roughly half of the binaries for primary masses of $10 M_\odot$, and favors nearly equal mass ratios overall; its spins are consistent with both black holes having negligible spin, with a log Bayes factor of $\log_{10}B =6.1^{+0.2}_{-0.3}$ in favor of vanishing spins. The medium-spin population accounts for the other half of the population around primary masses of $10 M_\odot$ and favors spin magnitudes $\chi_i \approx 0.2$ for both components, preferentially aligned orientations, and comparable mass ratios. The high-spin population dominates above primary masses of $60 M_\odot$ and also contributes at lower masses $\sim 20 M_\odot$; it favors a rapidly spinning primary ($\chi_1 \approx 0.7$), a broad range of secondary spins, widely distributed spin orientations, and a broad mass-ratio distribution. Allowing for a fourth subpopulation yields no distinct additional mass-ratio or spin distribution, as it becomes degenerate with existing features. To resolve highly concentrated features in spin, we control the variance of standard Monte Carlo likelihood estimators using truncated Gaussian mixture models. Taken together, our results add to a growing body of evidence for substructure in the population of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA black holes, providing further clues to uncover their formation histories.

new.title: ExoVetter and a TESS Exoplanet Transit Search of Kepler Stars as Ground Truth
new.summary: We introduce a Python package called exoVetter that produces vetting metrics and visualizations to evaluate transiting exoplanet signals found in high-cadence time-series photometry. exoVetter is open source, modular, and independent of the mission data so that it can be easily expanded and used as part of different transit search pipelines tuned to different science cases and missions. We demonstrate its use in a pipeline as a way to distinguish real events found in a box-least squares exoplanet transit search of 324,530 light curves from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite mission; we limit our demonstration to stars also observed by the more sensitive Kepler telescope as a way to establish ground truth for the events found in the light curves. Using this ground truth, we provide baseline thresholds for several flux-level vetters and one centroid-offset vetter when using exoVetter metrics on TESS data. Our demonstration also indicates that it is possible to create a planet catalog from the light curves of dim targets (>13.5Tmag) that has a similar fraction of real events to that of the bright targets (<13.5Tmag) for short period events identified in the TESS-Gaia light curves.

new.title: A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey
new.summary: Galaxy morphology traces the physical processes that shape galaxy evolution, but non-parametric diagnostic boundaries depend on image quality and preprocessing. We investigate the classification of regular spirals, regular ellipticals, mergers, and jellyfish (ram-pressure-stripping candidate) galaxies in the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Using galmex measurements of ten non-parametric morphological indices, we evaluate two-dimensional diagnostic planes with a cross-validated Bayesian kernel-density classifier and combine all indices using probability-calibrated LightGBM models. For separating regular spirals, regular ellipticals, and perturbed systems, the most informative planes combine Shannon entropy with $M_{20}$ or asymmetry indices, reaching balanced accuracies of 0.76-0.77. We provide survey-specific probabilistic boundaries in the entropy-$M_{20}$ and entropy-shape-asymmetry planes. Separating mergers from jellyfish candidates is more challenging; the best two-dimensional combinations, all involving concentration, reach balanced accuracies of approximately 0.73. The calibrated three-class LightGBM model achieves a balanced accuracy and macro-F1 score of 0.89, while the four-class model achieves 0.75 and 0.76, respectively. We provide class probabilities and preferred classifications for 1,744,454 galaxies. Our results show that non-parametric morphology identifies broad structural disturbance reliably, but distinguishing its physical origin is harder: jellyfish candidates occupy a relatively coherent region of parameter space, whereas mergers span diverse and overlapping morphologies.

new.title: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
new.summary: We present 14 optical imaging and eight optical spectroscopic epochs of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS from Keck/LRIS and Gemini/GMOS, two near-infrared (NIR) imaging epochs from Keck/MOSFIRE, and four NIR spectroscopic epochs from Gemini/Flamingos-2 and GNIRS, obtained between 2025 July and 2026 May. Mean GMOS colors of $g-r=0.732\pm0.029$, $r-i=0.237\pm0.025$, and $i-z=0.109\pm0.022$ mag show no significant change across perihelion. Phase-corrected red-band activity follows $Af\rho\propto r_h^{-2.10\pm0.14}$ inbound and $r_h^{-3.34\pm0.43}$ outbound. Transverse-width and sunward-plume speeds imply dust losses of $2.7\times10^9$ and $1.0\times10^{10}$ kg over 2025 July 3--2026 May 15 for 1-$\mu$m--1-mm grains, equivalent to global layers of 0.26 and 0.99 m under the adopted grain and nucleus assumptions. The concentrated coma, compact sunward feature, and antisolar tail seen on 2025 August 27 broadened by 2025 November 26; extended dust persisted through 2026 February 17. C$_2$/CN nearly doubled from $0.257\pm0.014$ on 2025 September 14--15 to $0.481\pm0.080$ on 2025 November 26, while C$_3$/CN fell from $0.327\pm0.024$ on 2025 August 28 to $0.214\pm0.009$ on 2025 September 14--15. MOSFIRE NIR imaging on 2025 July 11 gives $Y-J=0.466\pm0.143$, $J-H=0.239\pm0.052$, $H-K_s=0.454\pm0.150$, and $J-K_s=0.693\pm0.202$ mag. Spectra give $J-H=0.24$ mag on 2025 September 5--6 and $J-H=0.27$--0.28 and $J-K_s=0.21$--0.22 mag on 2025 December 1--2 over the retained passband intervals. Model-calibrated imaging on 2026 February 6 gives near-solar $J-K_s=0.303\pm0.051$ mag. No water-ice absorption is robust to the tested continuum and calibration choices in the NIR spectra. These observations provide a lasting record of the comet's evolution through the Solar System and a benchmark for studying and monitoring future interstellar objects.

cross.title: Impact of cosmic evolution on the gravitational wave spectrum from cosmic strings
cross.summary: In the standard cosmological paradigm, the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum from a cosmic string network is well defined. However, early-Universe dynamics can significantly alter this relic signal. We systematically investigate how different new physics epochs in the radiation era--including extra relativistic degrees of freedom, early matter domination, intermediate vacuum domination, and kination--modify string network evolution and loop production. We find that a kination era enhances the stochastic GW signal, whereas the other scenarios suppress the signal to varying degrees. We also demonstrate that late-time dynamical dark energy has a negligible impact on the GW spectrum from cosmic strings.

cross.title: Exceptional points and hysteresis in Kerr-Newman quasi-normal modes
cross.summary: Exceptional points (EPs) and eigenstate hysteresis, previously found in Kerr only with an auxiliary scalar field, arise intrinsically in the quasinormal-mode spectrum of Kerr-Newman black holes. Using a hyperboloidal formulation of the coupled gravito-electromagnetic Teukolsky equations and a Chebyshev pseudospectral method, we compute the $\ell=m=2$ spectrum and locate four EPs at up to $99.974\%$ of extremality, one from a new repulsion. The gaps close as a square root branch point, and quasistatic loops around one or more EPs exchange the coalescing modes, confirming hysteresis.

cross.title: Gravitational waves from inclined orbits around Kerr black holes
cross.summary: Extreme mass ratio inspirals on generic inclined orbits provide a critical dynamical probe of strong field gravity, as they uniquely break the severe parameter degeneracies inherent to planar equatorial trajectories. To isolate the exact rotational signatures, we extend the periodic-orbit framework to three-dimensional inclined trajectories in the Kerr spacetime, specifically focusing on the $r$--$\theta$ orbital resonances. By mapping the geodesic motion into a co-precessing spatial framework parameterized by Mino time, we compute the emitted quadrupole waveforms and evolve the local dynamics using circularity-preserving radiation reaction. It is demonstrated that frame-dragging induces a transient dynamical tilt at periastron, which directly splits the emitted radiation into an exact five-comb spectral architecture. When this resonant structure is resolved over a single coherence time, the statistical error on the dimensionless spin is reduced to $\sigma_a \approx 10^{-2}$, improving upon the equatorial baseline by up to two orders of magnitude. Because any bound orbit in a static, spherically symmetric spacetime generates a maximum of three frequency combs, the detection of this five-comb hierarchy establishes a rigorous, model-independent null test to strictly exclude spherical geometries.

cross.title: Non-Markovian Cosmology with Causal Memory Kernels
cross.summary: We investigate a non-Markovian extension of Friedmann cosmology in which the present expansion rate retains information about the past cosmic evolution through a causal memory kernel, with \LCDM{} recovered in the limit of vanishing kernel amplitude, $A\to0$. We show that five kernels (Linear, Power Law, Exponential, Gaussian and Oscillatory) arise as cosine transforms of the spectral densities of an unresolved hidden sector, and that the Exponential and Linear kernels also follow independently from Israel-Stewart causal viscosity and from Deser-Woodard non-local gravity, respectively. We constrain the kernels with 30 Cosmic Chronometer (CC) measurements and with $H(z)$ derived from the DESI DR1 and DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, using multi-start $\chi^{2}$ minimisation followed by Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling, and compare them with \LCDM{} through the Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. The Linear amplitude is consistent with zero ($A=0.002\pm0.030$ for CC+DR2). The Power-law, Exponential and Gaussian kernels are observationally degenerate: the data select sharply peaked kernels that constrain only an integrated amplitude $\Aeff\simeq0.01$--$0.03$, equivalent to a uniform $0.5$--$1.5\%$ rescaling of $H(z)$, and they are disfavoured relative to \LCDM{} ($\Delta{\rm AIC}=+2.5$ to $+3.6$). Only the Oscillatory kernel improves the fit appreciably ($\dchi=4.5$--$8.1$), but it requires a negative damping rate, which is incompatible with the causal derivations, and it is not favoured once CC data are included ($\Delta{\rm BIC}=+4.4$ to $+6.2$)

cross.title: Finite-distance effects and scalar suppression in massive gravity
cross.summary: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) probe the stochastic gravitational wave (GW) background through the angular cross-correlations of timing residuals. For a GW background in general relativity (GR), the expected overlap reduction function (ORF) is given by the Hellings--Downs (HD) correlation. We investigate how a nonzero graviton mass modifies this prediction through a massive dispersion relation and additional vector and scalar polarizations, producing a modified effective ORF. In the massive limit, the finite-distance pulsar terms survive angular averaging, multiplying the correlations of all three polarization sectors by a pulsar-dependent factor that can enhance, suppress, or reverse them. We adopt a tensor Earth--Earth normalization that preserves the continuous finite-distance effect. In the massless limit, we find that the vector ORF vanishes and the scalar ORF approaches a finite breathing mode. We propose the phenomenological prescription $\Omega_S/\Omega_T=A_S(m_g/\omega)^{n_S}$, with scalar amplitude parameter $A_S$ and suppression index $n_S>0$. These results provide a consistent framework for future PTA analyses of massive gravity.

cross.title: Magnetic field effect on neutral color superconductivity as a mechanism to boost the inner magnetic field of magnetars
cross.summary: In this paper, we review the impact of a strong magnetic field on the neutral two-flavor color superconducting (2SC) phase of dense quark matter. Using a Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model approach in the mean-field approximation, we first solve the gap equations for the diquark condensate $\Delta$ and the electric chemical potential $\mu_e$ under a uniform external magnetic field, and discuss the coupled evolution of the chiral and diquark order parameters. We then evaluate the field-dependent Meissner masses of the rotationally charged gluons for a wide range of densities and moderate diquark coupling strengths. Combining the "zero-mode problem" mechanism with the neutrality condition, we show that the gluon masses become tachyonic even at moderate magnetic-field values, signaling a chromomagnetic instability in density regions where the system was stable at zero field. This instability can be resolved through the restructuring of the ground state with the formation of a gluon vortex condensate. A remarkable consequence of the vortex configuration is the paramagnetic amplification of the in-medium magnetic field: seed fields of the order of $10^{15}$ G can be enhanced by up to two orders of magnitude, reaching $\sim 10^{17}$ G, precisely the range predicted for magnetar cores. We compare this microscopic mechanism with the conventional dynamo explanation and discuss how it offers a plausible explanation for the extremely high magnetic fields expected to be realized in magnetar interiors.

cross.title: Stochastic dynamics of cosmological inflation in general relativity
cross.summary: The theory of Inflation, supplemented by fluctuations of the quantum vacuum, is the leading paradigm to explain the correlations of inhomogeneities at very large distances in the Universe. Particle physics methods fail when strong non-linearity and non-perturbativity are involved, leaving a whole landscape of untestable scenarios of inflation. Starobinsky's stochastic inflation can in principle treat inflationary inhomogeneities nonlinearly and classically as the Hubble radius becomes smaller than their wavelengths, but it was never formulated in full general relativity, which motivates this thesis. Using the Keldysh formalism of nonequilibrium quantum field theory, we first develop a validity criterion for the use of classical computations, and thus simulations, to probe inflationary interactions, finding analytically that the bispectrum can be extracted from slightly sub-Hubble scales in quasi-de Sitter spacetimes. We then provide the first analytical solutions to the constraints for inhomogeneous initial conditions of numerical relativity simulations of inflation, and use them to explore its nonperturbative regime. Our main contribution is to obtain stochastic equations for the full set of inflaton equations in general relativity: this description incorporates the full nonlinear and backreacting evolution, is small-gauge-invariant, and is free of historical assumptions such as the gradient-free separate universe approximation. We implement these equations in the BSSN formulation of numerical relativity, demonstrating their correctness in slow-roll and ultra slow-roll scenarios via the satisfaction of the constraints, with a first look at eternal inflation. Finally, we extend our coarse-graining methods beyond General Relativity and single-field inflation, offering a phenomenological framework with the ambition of serving as a numerical particle collider for the early universe.

cross.title: Gauge-field energy density in inflationary kinetic-coupling models: QFT regularization versus horizon cutoffs
cross.summary: Coupling gauge fields to the inflaton can amplify their quantum fluctuations during inflation, with potential applications to a range of cosmological phenomena. A central challenge is to define finite and physically meaningful observables, such as the gauge-field energy density. In this work, we study an Abelian gauge field kinetically coupled to the inflaton through $f^2(\phi)F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}$ in a de Sitter background with $f\propto a^{\gamma_1}$, and compare conventional quantum-field-theoretic regularization with horizon-cutoff prescriptions. Using a hard physical-momentum cutoff and dimensional regularization, we derive the ultraviolet divergences in closed form and fix the remaining one-parameter finite-part ambiguity by requiring the coupling-induced total energy density to be nonnegative. We then examine five horizon-cutoff prescriptions based on characteristic scales of the mode equations. Their predictions depend sensitively on the choice of horizon scale and, for weak gauge-field production, can deviate substantially from the regularized result; for the adopted finite-part prescription, the minimal horizon agrees best with the regularized total energy density. As $|\gamma_1|\to 2$, where infrared modes dominate, the relative deviation of all prescriptions from the regularized result vanishes, independently of the finite-part prescription. Outside this regime, the separate electric and magnetic contributions, which can become negative after regularization, are not reliably reproduced by any of the horizon-cutoff prescriptions.

repl.title: Natural Inflation with Exponentially Small Tensor-To-Scalar Ratio
repl.summary: We demonstrate that "natural inflation", also known as "axion inflation", can be compatible with Planck 2018 measurements of the cosmic microwave background, while predicting an exponentially small tensor-to-scalar ratio, e.g., $r\sim 10^{-15}$. The strong suppression of $r$ arises from dynamics of the radial component of the complex scalar field, whose phase is the axion. Such tiny values of $r$ remain well below the threshold for detection by CMB-S4 or Simons Observatory B-mode searches. The model is testable with the running $\alpha_s$ of the spectral index, which is within reach of next-generation CMB and large-scale structure experiments, motivating the running as a primary science goal for future experiments.

repl.title: Euclid: Quick Data Release (Q1) -- Ultracool dwarfs in the Euclid Deep Fields
repl.summary: Ultracool dwarfs (UCDs) encompass the lowest-mass stars and brown dwarfs at the substellar boundary. These intrinsically faint objects are challenging to detect, but the wide coverage and deep sensitivity of the Euclid survey increase confirmed UCD counts by orders of magnitude. We carried out a systematic study using Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) low-resolution near-infrared spectra to identify and characterise UCDs. A sample of previously known UCDs in Q1 validated the analysis, which was then applied to newly identified UCD candidates in Euclid Deep Field North (EDF-N; 22.9 deg^2, down to J_E ~ 24.5 mag). We confirm 33 new UCDs in EDF-N, spanning spectral types M7-T1 (J_E = 17-21 mag) and distances of 50-600 pc. Two objects were followed up with optical and NIR observations using the Gran Telescopio Canarias, providing independent validation of Euclid classifications. We determined spectral types for 33 new UCDs and 167 previously known UCDs by fitting SpeX Prism Library Analysis Toolkit standards. The known sample includes 103 Dark Energy Survey objects (M7-T0, J_E = 17-22 mag), 6 literature sources (M8-T7, J_E = 18-20 mag), and 58 Gaia sources (M7-L1, J_E = 17-24 mag). Independent stellar parameters from atmospheric model fitting agree well with Euclid spectral types. We also investigated Gaia UCDs in Q1 by combining mean XP spectra with Euclid NIR spectra to determine radii. We present a publicly available catalogue including observations, classifications, and stellar parameters. This work demonstrates Euclid's capability to characterise faint stellar populations, establishing a foundation for large-scale UCD studies.

repl.title: Resilience of Primordial Black Hole Formation from Inflation with a Light Spectator Field
repl.summary: Scalar fields are ubiquitous in theories of high-energy physics. In the context of cosmic inflation, this suggests the existence of spectator fields, which provide a subdominant source of energy density. We show that spectator fields boost the inflationary production of primordial black holes, with single-field ultra-slow-roll evolution supplanted by a phase of evolution along the spectator direction, and primordial perturbations amplified by the resulting multifield dynamics. This generic mechanism is largely free from the severe fine-tuning that afflicts single-field inflationary PBH models.

repl.title: Tracing the evolution of eccentric precessing binary black holes: a hybrid approach
repl.summary: To describe a general bound binary black hole system, we need to consider orbital eccentricity and the misalignment of black holes' spin vectors with respect to the orbital angular momentum. Binary black holes often have a non-negligible eccentricity at formation, and dynamical interactions could produce binaries with non-negligible eccentricity in the bands of gravitational-wave (GW) detectors. The angle between each black hole's spin vector and the binary's orbital angular momentum (referred to as the spin tilt) at formation also carries information about the formation channel. The spin tilts inferred in GW astronomy are usually those when the binary is in the band of a GW detector. Therefore, it is necessary to evolve the binary back in time to compute the tilts at formation. For certain binaries, the tilts in the formal limit of infinite orbital angular momentum, also known as tilts at infinity, could be a useful approximation to those at formation. Additionally, full orbit-averaged evolution to formation could be computationally infeasible in many situations, while the hybrid evolution we use to compute the tilts at infinity would be feasible. We thus generalize the publicly available tilts_at_infinity code to compute the tilts at infinity for eccentric, spin-precessing binaries. This code employs hybrid post-Newtonian evolution, starting with orbit-averaged evolution for higher frequencies and then transitioning to precession-averaged evolution to compute the tilts at infinity. We find that the transition frequency used in the quasicircular case still gives acceptably small errors in the eccentric case, and show that eccentricity and hybrid evolution both have a significant effect on the tilts at infinity for many binaries. We also give examples of cases where the tilts at infinity are and are not a good approximation to the tilts at formation in the eccentric case. (Abridged)

repl.title: Testing the Correlations between X-ray Spectral Properties and Polarization for High Synchrotron Peaked Blazars
repl.summary: IXPE has enabled the X-ray polarizations of many blazars to be measured. We present the first population study for high synchrotron peaked blazars observed with IXPE using a uniform X-ray data analysis. We do not find any statistically significant correlations between the spectral properties of the blazars and their X-ray polarimetric properties. The lack of significant correlations may imply that there is little connection between the energy distribution of the X-ray emitting electrons and the uniformity of the magnetic field in the X-ray emitting regions of these blazars. These results will inform future theoretical work and potentially help narrow down the acceleration process of the synchrotron electrons.

repl.title: Primordial Black Holes from Inflation with a Spectator Field
repl.summary: How is the production of primordial black holes (PBHs) in single-field models of inflation impacted by the presence of additional scalar fields? We consider the effect of a spectator field - a free scalar field with sub-Hubble mass and no direct coupling to the inflaton and which makes a subdominant contribution to the total energy density - in the context of single-field models of inflation featuring a transient phase of ultra-slow-roll evolution. Despite the modest title, a spectator field can have a dramatic impact: the slow-roll evolution of the spectator prevents the combined inflaton-and-spectator system from entering into ultra-slow-roll, which naively might be expected to preclude the production of PBHs. However, we demonstrate that the growth of perturbations is maintained or enhanced by the spectator, through the rich interplay of curvature and isocurvature perturbations. We show in a model-independent way that the single-field phase of ultra-slow-roll is replaced by two turns in field space encompassing a phase of tachyonic instability for the isocurvature perturbations and a transfer of power from isocurvature to curvature modes. Furthermore, we highlight a degeneracy between the fine-tuning of the feature in the inflaton potential and the parameters of the spectator, leading to an overall resilience of model predictions to parameter variations. This makes it easier for the underlying PBH model to accommodate both high-precision cosmic microwave background constraints and production of PBHs in the asteroid-mass range.

repl.title: OmniSpectra: A Unified Foundation Model for Universal Spectra Representation Learning
repl.summary: Standard sequence models encode position by token rank rather than physical coordinate, typically forcing practitioners to destructively resample continuous physical signals such as spectra observed across heterogeneous instruments. We identify this coordinate mismatch as a structural limitation in cross-instrument representation learning, and propose OmniSpectra, a wavelength-native foundation model for spectral representation learning: a continuous-coordinate masked autoencoder that discards the integer pixel indexing of sequence modeling. Mapping physical coordinates to a logarithmic basis turns the multiplicative scaling induced by cosmological redshift into a uniform additive shift. In continuous rotary position embeddings, this shared shift cancels from relative token distances rather than producing grid-dependent positional distortion. We further counter the spectral bias inherent to implicit neural decoders with a physics-grounded, resolution-gated Fourier decoder that provides anti-aliasing. Pretrained on eight surveys and benchmarked against seven baselines, our model reaches state-of-the-art performance with only 12.2M parameters while outperforming substantially larger models, indicating that encoding physical structure can substitute for parameter scale.

repl.title: Cosmological Equivalence of Scalar-Tensor-Vector Modified Gravity and Cold Dark Matter
repl.summary: We show that Scalar-Tensor-Vector Gravity (STVG-MOG) is observationally equivalent to the standard model $\Lambda$CDM cosmological model for all probes that depend on isotropic and linear gravitational dynamics, including galaxy rotation curves, cluster lensing, the linear matter power spectrum P(k), $\sigma_8$, baryon acoustic oscillations, and the cosmic microwave background (CMB). This degeneracy arises from the scale-dependent effective gravitational coupling $G_{\mathrm{eff}}$, which ensures identical background evolution, transfer functions, and linear growth. Consequently, all early-universe, low and intermediate scale cosmological observables are equally well described by STVG-MOG without invoking non-baryonic dark matter. We argue that the equivalence implies that isotropic cosmological data alone cannot establish the physical existence of dark matter. The degeneracy is broken only by observables sensitive to large-scale, anisotropic gravitational response. In particular, recent measurements of enhanced radio-galaxy and quasar number-count dipoles at gigaparsec scales probe a regime where $G_{\mathrm{eff}}$ departs from its $\Lambda$CDM limit, allowing STVG-MOG to generate anisotropic bulk flows, while preserving consistency with all isotropic constraints. These observations provide a concrete pathway for empirically distinguishing modified gravity from particle dark matter.

repl.title: Kinematic cosmic dipole from a large sample of strong lenses
repl.summary: Measurements of the kinematic cosmic dipole continue to show an intriguing tension between the value inferred from the CMB and that obtained from high-redshift source number counts. While the measured dipole direction appears consistent, the amplitude, set by the observer's peculiar velocity $v_{o}$, remains in significant disagreement. In this paper, we propose using strong gravitational lenses with well-measured Einstein radii to estimate the kinematic cosmic dipole, through the relativistic aberration of the Einstein angle induced by the observer's motion. We show that this effect could be detected solely from measurements of the Einstein radius in wide, high-resolution imaging surveys such as Euclid. However, the precision achievable using Einstein-radius measurements alone, without redshift or lens-galaxy mass information, appears insufficient to discriminate between the CMB value of $v_{o}$ and that derived from source number counts at high statistical significance. Nevertheless, we demonstrate that including a large sample of lenses with available kinematic information, either via the Fundamental Plane relation or, ideally, through spectroscopic velocity-dispersion measurements, drastically reduces the noise and substantially improves the constraining power of this method. We show that, for a realistic sample of strong lenses detected by Euclid and complemented with spectroscopic velocity dispersion measurements from 4MOST or DESI, it is possible to discriminate between the CMB- and source-number-counts-inferred values at the $\sim 5\sigma$ level using a new, fully independent method. We further demonstrate that this technique is only weakly sensitive to strong-lensing selection effects, with selection biases and threshold effects estimated to be well below the 1% level.

repl.title: Quantitative modelling of type Ia supernovae spectral time series II: Exploring the diversity of thermonuclear explosion scenarios
repl.summary: Observations of type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) have led to suggestions of multiple progenitor and explosion scenarios. Distinguishing between scenarios and tying specific SNe Ia to individual scenarios however has so far been challenging. Constraints on the explosion physics are often achieved through empirical modelling of SNe Ia spectra and qualitative assessments of the level of agreement. While this approach has provided useful insights, it cannot be scaled up to large numbers of SNe Ia in a robust and systematic way. As a machine learning based framework for automated and quantitative fitting of SNe Ia, riddler is designed to overcome these limitations. Neural networks are used as radiative transfer emulators and, in conjunction with nested sampling, emulated spectra are fit to observations of SNe Ia to determine the best-fitting input parameters and explosion scenario. In this work, we present recent improvements to riddler, including a significantly expanded training dataset covering pure deflagrations, delayed detonations, double detonations, gravitationally confined detonations, and violent mergers. We show that despite the increased complexity and variety of our training data, riddler is able to accurately recover the input parameters and explosion scenario of spectra unseen during training. Using riddler, we fit observations of three SNe Ia covering different sub-classes: SN 2011fe, SN 2005hk, and SN 2018byg. We detail a number of limitations and assumptions that should be considered when applying similar approaches. Nevertheless, the benefits of this approach and riddler will result in automated fitting playing an increasingly important role in the coming years.

repl.title: Toward Bayesian photometric cosmic chronometers: Application to VIPERS
repl.summary: The cosmic chronometer (CC) method provides a direct measurement of the expansion history of the universe, $H(z)$, from the differential ages of passively evolving galaxies. However, most CC analyses rely on high-quality spectroscopy to select passive galaxies, measure age-sensitive spectral features, and control stellar-population systematics. We build on existing works that use the D4000 spectral break as a proxy for measuring galaxy ages and apply it to a photometry-selected galaxy sample from VIPERS PDR2 in the range $0.5 \le z \le 0.8$. Our goal is to extend the scope of the standard CC framework to photometric surveys. To achieve this, we first selected a massive and passive galaxy sample using rest-frame colors and mass. Second, we designed a Bayesian framework to infer full galaxy age posteriors in fine redshift bins, using a D4000-age-metallicity grid from stellar population synthesis models. We marginalized over metallicity, using a Gaussian metallicity prior to break the D4000-age-metallicity degeneracy. Subsequently, we derived age-difference posteriors between redshift bins by convolving their age posteriors. Finally, using the median and errors extracted from the differential age posteriors, we calculated the weighted average $H(z)$ over our selected redshift range. We obtain $H(z=0.65)=93.68\pm28.27\,{\rm (stat.)}\pm10.67\,{\rm (syst.)}\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, which is consistent with existing spectroscopic CC measurements and with the $\Lambda$ cold dark matter ($\Lambda$CDM) model prediction from Planck at the same redshift. This result provides a proof of concept for extending direct $H(z)$ measurements from cosmic chronometers to photometric and spectro-photometric surveys, where larger samples can compensate for lower spectral resolution, provided that passive-galaxy selection, metallicity priors, and stellar-population systematics are carefully controlled.

repl.title: Stellar Population Spectra Incorporating Detailed Binary Evolution using POSYDON
repl.summary: The accuracy of stellar population properties inferred through spectral energy distribution fitting hinges on the reliability of the underlying spectral models. Binary interactions are fundamental for massive star evolution, and ignoring their spectral contribution can lead to incorrect results. We use the POSYDON binary population synthesis code to generate spectral models of stellar populations that include binaries at solar metallicity. Our framework incorporates a collection of spectral libraries that is designed to address key outcomes of binary stellar evolution like Wolf-Rayet stars, stripped helium stars, and a treatment for stellar mergers. Our models confirm previous results showing that the inclusion of binary interactions has a significant effect on the UV and ionizing regime of the integrated spectrum. In particular we find that Wolf-Rayet stars and other massive stars dominate the production of ionizing radiation at earlier times, but after $\simeq$16 Myr stripped stars produced through mass transfer begin to dominate. Furthermore, we show that the production of ionizing He II photons is especially sensitive to the underlying population of stripped stars. While our results currently focus on high-mass stars ($\ge4~M_{\odot}$) at Solar metallicity, they provide the framework for binary spectral synthesis across a range of metallicities and masses and lay the foundation for calculations of the emergent emission-line spectra in the UV, optical, and IR regimes. We make the spectral models from this work publicly available for use in a format that can be integrated into fitting codes.

repl.title: UCLCHEM 4.0: An open source gas-grain astrochemistry simulation framework
repl.summary: Astrochemical modelling is a key tool for interpreting the formation and destruction of molecules in the interstellar medium, complementing the increasingly detailed observations enabled by modern day observational facilities. UCLCHEM is a comprehensive gas-grain astrochemical modelling framework that can compute the chemical evolution inside a parcel of gas and dust under a specified, time-dependent physical description. This allows both the post-processing of hydrodynamical simulations and the usage of physical parametrizations, ranging in context from extra-galactic to protoplanetary disk scales. The framework consists of a core routine that solves gas-grain chemical reaction networks as a function of time, self-consistently coupled to either a user-defined or parametrized physical evolution of density, temperature and other physical input parameters. The chemistry is solved with a rate-equation formalism, and includes a three phase description, namely gas phase, ice surface and bulk ice. This includes transport between the gas and ice phases via freeze-out, thermal and non-thermal desorption mechanisms, as well as a geometrical treatment of the growth and shrinkage of the surface and bulk chemistry. The framework includes parametrizations for astrochemical modelling of cloud collapses, protostellar cores and shocks as well as the ability to provide user-defined inputs. This release of the framework focuses on many quality-of-life-improvements, including an object-oriented Python interface, an upgrade from two phase to three phases and expanded support for post-processing of hydrodynamical simulations and user-defined parametrizations. This manuscript provides an overview of the physics and chemistry included in UCLCHEM, as well as the inner workings of the solver routine and the programming interface.

repl.title: The Best Guess: Testing new and old formalisms for the common envelope against observations
repl.summary: We present a systematic test of formalisms for common envelope evolution by forward-modelling observable post-common envelope binaries. We compare predictions from the $\alpha$-formalism, and the Two-stage and SCATTER formalisms against observed post-common envelope binaries, including wide binaries with ultra-massive white dwarfs and central binaries of planetary nebulae. The angular momentum-based SCATTER formalism does not predict populations which match the complete observed population, even with adjustments to its parameters. We take this as indicative of fundamental challenges with using the orbital angular momentum balance to predict common envelope outcomes. The energy-based $\alpha $ and hybrid Two-stage formalisms both well-replicate the observed population. $\alpha_{\rm CE} \sim 0.2\text{--}0.3$ can match current observations, in agreement with previous works. Recombination energy is necessary, but only a fraction of it ($\sim\! 10\text{--}40\%$) can contribute in order to predict IK Peg-like binaries with ultra-massive white dwarfs at the correct orbital periods. Our work suggests energy-based formalisms remain the most accurate for predicting common envelope outcomes, but more observations can constrain the recombination contribution and how these outcomes systematically vary with the donor mass.

repl.title: What visibility-graph curvature measures in Forbush decreases: a calibration on the two largest events of solar cycle 25
repl.summary: Discrete curvatures of visibility graphs are increasingly used as descriptors of geophysical time series, but their response to a transient has rarely been calibrated against the simplest properties of that transient. We carry out this calibration for the nodal Forman--Ricci curvature $\mathcal{F}$ of natural visibility graphs applied to neutron-monitor records of the Gannon storm (2024 May 10--11) and the 2025 June 1 Forbush decrease (FD), the two largest FDs of solar cycle 25, using 30-min NMDB data from six NM64 stations ($R_c \simeq 0$--$7$~GV), i.e.\ twelve station--event series. Curvature collapses at FD onset in every series (Cliff's $\delta = 0.63$--$1.0$), but a 6-h running standard deviation separates onset from quiet time more strongly (mean $\delta = 0.96$ vs $0.89$; mean block-permutation displacement $z = -27$ vs $-14$). Injecting synthetic decreases into the real pre-event records of each station shows that the curvature extreme follows $|\mathcal{F}_{\min}| \propto (A/\sigma)^{0.50}$ ($R^2 = 0.88$), where $A$ is the FD amplitude and $\sigma$ the station's quiet-time noise, and is independent of the duration of the main phase (exponent $0.006$ over 3--36~h). With $A$, $\sigma$ and the main-phase duration of each series as the only inputs, the calibration predicts the twelve observed extremes with standardized residuals of mean $-0.26$ and standard deviation $0.94$, and the observed extremes correlate with $A/\sigma$ at Spearman $\rho = 0.95$. Within the precision allowed by these data, nodal Forman--Ricci curvature of the whole-series visibility graph carries no information about these FDs beyond their amplitude relative to station noise; in particular, it does not distinguish the single-step Gannon decrease from the two-step June 2025 decrease.

repl.title: Even central galaxies feel their environment: cosmic siphoning of cool gas accretion
repl.summary: Identifying the key processes regulating cool gas accretion in galaxies is essential for understanding the baryon cycle within galactic ecosystems. Recent studies indicate that the most fundamental internal process is likely the competition between halos and central black holes. This is revealed through a universal relation between increasing black hole masses and decreasing cool gas fraction ($\mu_{\rm HI} \equiv M_{\rm HI}/M_{\star} \propto M_{\rm BH}^{-0.6}$). Here we further explore the primary external effects on cool gas accretion in central galaxies. We find that galaxies deviating significantly from the $\mu_{\rm HI}-M_{\rm BH}$ relation are overwhelmingly isolated central galaxies without substantial satellites. These isolated, gas-poor centrals exhibit systematically higher black-hole-to-stellar-mass ratios and more prominent bulges. At larger scales, they are preferentially located near massive neighboring halos. We suggest that this may reflect a ``cosmic siphoning" scenario, replenished by their satellites and by gas flowing along the cosmic web. This model naturally explains the prevalence of gas-poor isolated central galaxies near massive halos. It complements internal regulation by supermassive black holes and suggests a cosmic 'rich get richer' scenario.

repl.title: Effective reheating in Gauss--Bonnet inflation with $μ(ϕ,X)$ coupling
repl.summary: We study effective reheating in a scalar--Gauss--Bonnet inflationary model with a phase-space-dependent coupling $\mu(\phi,X)$, in which a compact field-space feature is combined with a bounded kinetic gate. The modified inflationary background determines the pivot-scale quantities and the effective energy density at the end of inflation. These quantities are then used to derive the reheating duration $N_{\rm re}$ and temperature $T_{\rm re}$ through the thermal-history matching relation. We first perform two fixed-pivot reference scans by varying the overall Gauss--Bonnet strength $\lambda_{\rm GB}$ and the kinetic parameter $g_{_X}$ separately. For the reference parameter choices, increasing either parameter increases $N_{\rm re}$ and decreases $T_{\rm re}$ for the selected reheating equations of state. Additional benchmark calculations clarify how these variations depend on the dynamical regime of the model. In the $\lambda_{\rm GB}$ scan, the increase in $N_{\rm re}$ and the decrease in $T_{\rm re}$ persist, although both variations become strongly suppressed when the coupling is more localized or when the end of inflation is controlled more strongly by the E-model potential. In the $g_{_X}$ scan, stronger field-space localization and kinetic saturation can instead lead to a slight decrease in $N_{\rm re}$ and an increase in $T_{\rm re}$ as $g_{_X}$ is increased. When the bounded kinetic contribution is considered together with a weaker overall Gauss--Bonnet interaction, the resulting changes in the reheating quantities become nearly negligible. The fixed-pivot predictions of the representative and alternative benchmarks are compared with CMB this http URL reheating constraints are then discussed for four representative values of the effective equation-of-state parameter, $\overline{w}_{\rm re}=-1/3,0,2/3,$ and $1$.

repl.title: Astrophysical Constraints on Hadron--Quark Crossover in Hybrid Neutron Stars
repl.summary: We investigate astrophysical constraints on hybrid neutron-star equations of state constructed by combining an extended linear sigma model description of quark matter with several representative hadronic equations of state through a smooth hadron--quark crossover. Four different hadronic models are examined in order to explore the model dependence of the resulting hybrid equations of state. After imposing stability, causality, perturbative QCD matching, tidal deformability, and maximum-mass constraints, only the eLSM+GMSR(BSK16) construction remains fully consistent with current astrophysical observations. The surviving parameterizations are further constrained using Bayesian inference based on NICER mass--radius measurements and the GW170817 gravitational-wave event. The posterior distributions favor a broad hadron--quark crossover occurring at relatively high baryon densities, while the formation of extended pure quark cores is strongly disfavored. Instead, the current observations favor neutron stars containing an extended mixed hadron--quark transition region. We also investigate the implications of the inferred maximum-mass distribution for the secondary object of GW190814 and find that, within the present model and adopted observational constraints, its interpretation as a neutron star is unlikely.

repl.title: Decoupling candidate dual AGN from chance superpositions in the GOTHIC survey via a deep-learning framework
repl.summary: Dual active galactic nuclei (DAGN) mark a critical phase in the evolution of merging galaxies and the pairing of supermassive black holes, yet they remain difficult to identify in large imaging surveys because of projection effects and limited spatial resolution. Compact foreground stars and unresolved substructure can mimic dual nuclei through chance superposition, complicating automated detection. We revisit the 46,061 galaxies flagged but rejected as DAGN candidates by the GOTHIC pipeline, primarily because the two nuclei fell within the SDSS fibre aperture or exceeded its separation threshold. We train a supervised deep-learning framework based on the YOLOv11 oriented-bounding-box architecture on annotated SDSS imaging to separate genuine dual nuclei from foreground stellar contaminants and other spurious alignments. The final model attains a validation precision of 0.919, recall of 0.905, and $F_1$ of 0.912, and yields 29,605 dual-nucleus candidates after removing star-dominated and blended detections. Structured visual inspection indicates that $54.5$--$62\%$ are consistent with genuine dual nuclei, implying $\sim(1.4$--$1.8)\times10^{4}$ plausible systems. Cross-calibrating the YOLO separation against the deterministic GOTHIC centroid measurement and restricting to the compact regime ($d \le 6.87''$) gives a conservative subset of $\sim 13{,}672$ candidates, reaching calibrated separations of $\sim 0.56''$. Spectroscopy of the most compact ($\le 1$ kpc) systems shows spectra dominated by stellar absorption, with no resolved double-peaked emission, so confirmation requires higher-resolution follow-up. The catalogue is a statistically refined list of candidates, not confirmed DAGN. Nonetheless, deep-learning detection substantially reduces contamination and expands the plausible DAGN census.

repl.title: AXIS Could Have Accessed Dark Matter Decays
repl.summary: The Advanced X-ray Imaging Satellite (AXIS) was a mission concept designed to improve upon the sensitivity and spatial resolution of the Chandra X-ray Observatory and XMM-Newton. Although AXIS was not selected for implementation, the concept study defined a mature instrument design with low-background, arcsecond imaging over the $0.3$-$10$ keV energy range, a large effective area, and a wide field of view. These capabilities provide a useful benchmark for the dark matter decay sensitivity of future X-ray observatories. We estimate the reach of a future AXIS-like instrument for narrow photon lines from decaying keV-scale dark matter, including axion-like particles and sterile neutrinos. For Galactic center observations, we find projected lifetime sensitivities of order $10^{31}$ s, improving upon existing limits by up to an order of magnitude over part of the keV mass range.

repl.title: Tracing the Cosmic Origins: Machine Learning Reconstruction of the Primordial Density Field from EoR Observations
repl.summary: Reconstructing the initial conditions of the Universe from late-time tracers would unlock cosmological information buried by non-linear structure formation and astrophysics. We reconstruct the initial density field corresponding to $z=300$, with its linear amplitude extrapolated to $z=0$, from simulated 21-cm and CO(1-0) line-intensity maps at $z=8$ generated with LIMFAST. Using a three-dimensional U-Net, we reconstruct the initial conditions and evaluate their impact on cosmological parameter constraints. The two tracers probe complementary environments: 21-cm emission traces neutral, low-density regions of the IGM, while CO traces overdense, star-forming regions. We also train and evaluate the reconstruction on maps incorporating SKA1-Low- and COMAP-ERA-like instrumental response and thermal noise. In the noiseless case, combining both tracers delivers the most accurate reconstruction across ionisation states, with the cross-correlation coefficient between the reconstructed and true initial density fields, $|C(k)| \gtrsim 0.90$ for $k \lesssim 0.75\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. With observational effects, small-scale information is degraded, but the joint reconstruction retains substantial large-scale coherence, with $|C(k)| \gtrsim 0.70$ for $k \lesssim 0.3\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. We quantify cosmological information gains through simulation-based inference using power-spectrum summaries pre- and post-reconstruction. The largest improvements occur for $\sigma_8$ and $n_{\rm s}$, with a median aggregate marginal compression of $1.17$ bits in the noiseless case, corresponding to a $56\%$ reduction in the factorised product of prior-normalised $68\%$ marginal widths. With observational effects, the corresponding median compression is $1.29$ bits. These results demonstrate that joint 21-cm-CO reconstruction recovers cosmological information beyond pre-reconstruction summaries.
